character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity curled beneath the world's bones that dreamed Aethrea into being. It stirred, and its unbroken ten-thousand-year dream-song snapped like a struck bell, tearing the six kingdoms apart into drifting debris in a void of raw magic. It now dreams a broken, dividing nightmare somewhere in the depths, no longer in contact with the scattered world.

past_events.description: During the Shattering, Kaelen's uncontrollable fire spread through the Cathedral of the First Flame, killing pilgrims including a woman clinging to the altar rail and an acolyte who died crying Kaelen's name. He forgot the cathedral was full because he was lost in his own shame; their faces now haunt him.

future_requirements.description: Kaelen must find a reason to continue living; his search is answered when he scavenges the Ember-Scar's ruin and finds the shattered prophecy-stone in the next chapter.
Kaelen's drifting cinder sails the void until it collides with a drowned fragment of Tidal, forcing him ashore on an alien, silent water world.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer after his uncontrollable flame burned the Cathedral of the First Flame during the Shattering, killing pilgrims (including a woman at the altar rail and an acolyte who died crying his name). Now ashore on a drowned, silent fragment of Tidal — a black coral-crusted spire lying on its side, sheathed in freezing black water — after his slag-and-flame raft collided with its edge and threw him clear. He carries the two halves of the shattered prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry, warm against his chest; the stone's fractured edge grows hot and tugs toward the direction the world tore, and its First Script message says six unbounded souls, one from each fallen kingdom, must not fight the World-Titan but wake it gently and weave a new world-key ('the key is not the lock; the key is the song'). He has no faith but has chosen to act, driven by the faces of the dead and his promise to find a reason to go on. His goal is to follow the prophecy-stone and find the other souls, if they exist. His hands are burned black to the wrists and weeping; he is hungry, thirsty, exhausted, and guilt-haunted, but his fire burns low and stubborn as a beacon. He can shape cooled slag with his flame and coax it to push his raft through the void when too tired to fight it.

future_requirements.description: Kaelen must explore the drowned, silent fragment of Tidal and find whatever waits in its depths; the drowned spire holds a survivor of the Shattering who will test him (the tidecaller Nerys, merged with a living sea).
The prophecy-stone that warms toward the torn world must be shown to respond to the presence of other unbounded souls; it will hum in Nerys's presence when Kaelen tells her of it.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heretical belief that water must flow, not obey, rather than be ordered, channeled, and dammed to serve the kingdom. During the Shattering she survived by merging her consciousness with the living sea of her drowned spire fragment; she exists as a water-shape and current rather than a body, with a soft green inner light, and is reluctant and afraid to become a body again. Ancient, grieving, furious, and desperately lonely in the silence of the dead water world. Nearly drowned Kaelen to test him; after he confessed his fear of his own fire, she agreed to join his quest on one absolute condition: she will never be dammed again, or she will take the sea and drown him. She is the only one who remembers how water moves and can navigate the drowned currents of the Shattering, guiding their travel through the void. Their alliance is uneasy — fire and water circling each other — and she keeps herself flowing ahead of him in a silver current.

Small, hair cropped close, pale gray eyes glittering with hunger, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, clothes patched scraps of sanctified white. Wary of prophecy but recognized the prophecy-stone's words from Zephyr's old wind-cantor songs (six unbounded souls, wake the Titan gently, weave a new key). She joined the quest not out of duty but desperate freedom — a chance to fly somewhere no border can hold her — and gives the group speed, aerial skill, and a reckless hope that troubles Kaelen as much as it inspires him. Currently flying ahead of the raft, spiraling bright above Kaelen and Nerys as the three head toward Terra.

She flies ahead of the raft, spiraling bright, giving the group of four speed and aerial skill, heading toward the last two souls.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man in plates of dark stone that had grown onto him like a second skin, beard like a landslide, eyes the color of buried things. He kept vigil for an age over a field of hundreds of tombs of fallen kin on the last mountain remnant, armed with a great stone maul, convinced his world was still whole. The stone armor was the physical form of his denial; when Kaelen burned away its hairline seam he collapsed into grief and purposelessness, kneeling among the ruins of his kin. Kaelen offered him a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone — and Toren knelt and swore by the earth that is gone and the earth that may yet be, binding himself to a mission instead of a land. He now carries his great maul slung across his back and travels with the group as the fourth of six souls, his steadfast presence grounding them; he has stepped onto Kaelen's raft without looking back at the tombs, heading toward the last two souls.

She sees the luminous threads binding all things and will join them as the fifth unbounded soul, weaving a soft radiance.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man who once wore plates of dark stone that grew onto him as the armor of denial; after Kaelen burned away its hairline seam he collapsed into grief, then knelt and swore a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone — binding himself to a mission instead of a land. character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen, the fifth unbounded soul. She lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering — the same moment the prophecy-stone sang to her — and wears her blindness the way Toren wore his stone: as something she grew. In blindness she sees more truly: the luminous threads that bind all things, every soul a knot of light, every oath and grief a thread. She waited alone in the shattered ring of Lumen's Prism Cathedral (the Broken Lighthouse), keeping the dead lamp turned, serene and certain, and greeted the four champions like an answered prayer. She calmly explained they cannot reach the World-Titan by force — it is dreaming, and a dream must be answered with a song, confirming 'the key is not the lock, the key is the song.' She joined the group as its fifth soul, weaving a soft radiance that makes the void feel briefly like a shelter, and she knows the last soul waits in the dark where Umbra fell: more afraid and alone than any of them, unaware that he is a note at all.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity curled beneath the world's bones that dreamed Aethrea into being. It now dreams a broken, dividing nightmare somewhere in the depths. The shadow that infected Vex as a child remembers the Titan's dream-song when it was whole, and has been pouring that memory into Vex ever since.

character_states.name: Kaelen

He crossed the void on his raft of re-fired slag guided by the two halves of the shattered prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry; the stone has now sung for all six souls. He insisted Vex is an archive, not an abomination, and reached out his burned hands in friendship; Vex took them and agreed to guide the group. character_states.name: Nerys

Her one absolute condition stands: she will never be dammed again. In the Shadow Wound her current went thin and her green light guttered as the dark pressed in, but she linked hands with the others and descended. She now travels with all six unbounded souls (Kaelen, Nerys, Cyra, Toren, Elyra, Vex), leaving the Shadow Wound together, heading toward the Dreaming Heart. She is watchful of Vex's shadow but said nothing against him when Kaelen knelt.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete before she was branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights. In the Shadow Wound her breath went sharp and quick in the absolute dark and she almost bolted before Elyra told them to hold onto one another. She now travels with all six unbounded souls (Kaelen, Nerys, Cyra, Toren, Elyra, Vex), leaving the Shadow Wound together, heading toward the Dreaming Heart. She calls Elyra's light a lantern, not a lighthouse.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man who once wore plates of dark stone that grew onto him as the armor of denial; after Kaelen burned away its hairline seam he collapsed into grief, then knelt and swore a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone. He carries his great maul slung across his back. In the Shadow Wound his stone plates ground as he braced, and when Kaelen stepped toward Vex he gripped Kaelen's shoulder to warn him, then let him go. He now travels with all six unbounded souls (Kaelen, Nerys, Cyra, Toren, Elyra, Vex), leaving the Shadow Wound together, heading toward the Dreaming Heart.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen, the fifth unbounded soul, who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things, every soul a knot of light. In the Shadow Wound her lantern light was eaten by the absolute dark, but she stayed perfectly still and calm, telling the others the dark cannot take what it cannot separate; she was the first to name Vex and to see that he is a knot of light wrapped in shadow, not made of it. She now travels with all six unbounded souls (Kaelen, Nerys, Cyra, Toren, Elyra, Vex), leaving the Shadow Wound together, heading toward the Dreaming Heart to answer the Titan's dream with a song.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra, infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams. Small, curled into the smallest shape, grey skin mottled with veins of moving blackness; his eyes are two pools of absolute black behind which something vast and ancient sometimes looks out. The shadow speaks through him in a voice not his own, telling him things that have not yet happened; it once called Kaelen by his true name and told him it does not blame him for the burning. He was locked in the dark by Umbra and believed himself an abomination, but he revealed to Kaelen that he is an archive — the shadow is not evil but memory, pouring the whole dream-song of the world into him because there was no one else to hold it. He now travels with all six unbounded souls (Kaelen, Nerys, Cyra, Toren, Elyra, Vex), leaving the Shadow Wound together, heading toward the Dreaming Heart. His joining made the prophecy-stone sing its sixth and final note.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams — an archive of everything the world forgot. Small, grey skin mottled with moving black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which something vast sometimes looks out. During the Confluence battle the violence confirmed his old terror of being a weapon, but he stayed. In the Mirror of Fractures the shadow settled around him like a cloak he is learning to wear, and the Titan's dreaming voice spoke through him — chaos is not the enemy; the enemy is the lie that any single element can rule alone. He whispered 'The dream remembers being whole. It is waiting for us to remember with it.' He descends with all six souls toward the Dreaming Heart, guiding them through the shadows he has always feared.

past_events.description: During the Shattering, Kaelen's uncontrollable fire spread through the Cathedral of the First Flame, killing pilgrims including a woman clinging to the altar rail and an acolyte who died crying Kaelen's name. He forgot the cathedral was full because he was lost in his own shame; their faces now haunt him.

Scavenging the scorched wreck of the Ember-Scar cathedral that drifted with him, Kaelen found the shattered prophecy-stone, split cleanly in two by the Shattering, half-buried near the ruined altar dais. Its First Script inscription speaks of six unbounded souls, one from each fallen kingdom, who must not fight the World-Titan but wake it gently and weave a new world-key; the final line reads 'The key is not the lock. The key is the song.' The stone's fractured edges grow warm and tug toward the direction the world tore, serving him as a compass. He built a raft of re-fired slag shaped like a shallow skiff, propelled by his flame, and crossed the void until the stone led him to a fragment of Tidal.

On the drowned Tidal spire, Kaelen found Nerys, a tidecaller exiled for her heresy that water must flow not obey, who survived the Shattering by merging her consciousness with the living sea of the fragment. The prophecy-stone sang in her presence, confirming her as one of the six unbounded souls. She attacked him, nearly drowning him, and he confessed his terror of being an uncontrollable weapon of fire. She agreed to join him on one condition: no one will ever dam her again. He swore it. She now travels as a flowing current ahead of him, navigating the drowned currents of the Shattering — their first alliance is uneasy, fire and water circling each other.

At the Gyre Bastion, the broken Zephyr sky-fortress spinning out of control, the prophecy-stone sang for Cyra, the disgraced wind-rider. Nerys confronted her with the truth that endless flight without a destination is a cage without bars. Torn between desperate freedom and longing for somewhere no border can hold her, Cyra agreed to join, becoming the third unbounded soul; the group now numbers three of six, traveling with her speed and aerial skill.

Cyra recognized the prophecy-stone's inscription: Zephyr's old wind-cantors sang of six unbounded souls, waking the Titan gently and weaving a new key, as a lesson teaching children to obey and stay within the sanctified heights. This confirms the prophecy was known across the fallen kingdoms before the Shattering, and that she flew beyond those borders anyway.

After Cyra joined, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from the Gyre Bastion toward the slow dark where Terra's last mountain drifts — a mountain remnant where a stonewarden keeps vigil over the dead — setting the group's next heading.

On Terra, for the first time since the Shattering, Kaelen's fire acted with precision rather than blind rage: he lanced a hairline seam in the stone armor that had grown onto Toren — armor that was the physical form of his denial — and burned the scab of it away, shattering the denial and freeing Toren to grieve. This marks the first moment his flame aimed at healing instead of destruction.

After his denial was burned away, Toren the stonewarden knelt in grief and purposelessness among the tombs of his kin. Kaelen offered him a new oath — to protect the people trying to build a new world, not a mountain already gone — and Toren swore by the earth that is gone and the earth that may yet be, binding himself to a mission instead of a land. He took up his great maul and joined the group as the fourth of six souls.

After Toren joined the group, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from Terra's drifting mountain toward the deep dark where Lumen's broken light and Umbra's shadow await — the last two unbounded souls — setting the group's next heading.

Elyra lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering — the same moment the prophecy-stone sang to her. The prophecy-stone was cut from the same crystal as Lumen's Prism Cathedral, when the World-Titan's dream was whole; her blindness lets her see the luminous threads that bind all things, and she can perceive each soul as a knot of light bearing its oaths, griefs, and acts.

Elyra calmly explained that the champions will not reach the World-Titan by force: it is neither awake nor asleep but dreaming, and a dream cannot be fought with blade, maul, fire, or wind; it must be answered with a song. This unsettled Kaelen, who had come to expect violence and hardship at every landing, and reaffirmed the prophecy's line 'the key is not the lock. The key is the song.'

Vex of Umbra, the last unbounded soul, was infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dream-song when it was whole. The shadow is not evil but memory; it pours the forgotten dream-song into Vex and speaks through him in a voice not his own, telling him things that have not yet happened. Umbra locked him in the dark, calling him an abomination. He revealed he is an archive of everything the world forgot.

Inside the Shadow Wound, the shadow speaking through Vex called Kaelen by his true name — 'Kaelen of the First Flame' — in a vast, ancient voice that was not Vex's own, telling him it does not blame him for the burning of the cathedral. The voice terrified the group and confirmed the shadow's prophetic memory.

Recognizing in Vex the same fear he carries of being an uncontrollable weapon, Kaelen knelt and insisted Vex is an archive, not an abomination, offering his burned hands in friendship. Vex took them and agreed to guide the group through the shadows he has always feared, becoming the sixth unbounded soul. The prophecy-stone sang its sixth and final note — a swallowed, echoed note that joined the other five in the first chord of the new song.

After the Confluence battle, with the champions turning on one another, Elyra spoke the truth that cut through their fury: the Wardens of the First Facet did not need to kill them, only to make them forget they are one thing with six edges — and their rage at one another proved the Wardens right. This is the seed of the reconciliation to come: they must see themselves as one being with six broken edges, not six separate weapons.

The Wardens of the First Facet were not destroyed at the Fractured Confluence. Nerys's water-wraith drowned, folded over, and scattered them into the void — alive, robbed of their shapes — and shattered their sacrifice-gate of salvaged stone, bone, and dark mortar. Their zealotry survives in the dark and they may reassemble, still believing the old kingdoms must be forced back into rigid form through blood sacrifice.

At the Confluence, the Wardens chained Nerys in sea-iron etched with old Tidal glyphs that dammed her with written water — the second damming of her life. Held helpless, she took the full weight of Kaelen's uncontrolled fire, which nearly unmade her and drove her into the towering water-wraith. The violation of her one absolute condition has left her raw, furious, and unable to look at Kaelen, cracking the group's fragile unity.

In the aftermath of the Mirror of Fractures, Kaelen crossed the Confluence hub to Nerys without reaching for her — he had learned enough about damming to know he must never reach without invitation — opened his burned hands at his sides, and asked to carry the next piece with her: 'I am a shard, and so are you, and shards fit.' Nerys warned him that if he ever boiled her again she would take him to the bottom with her; he answered 'I will go.' The cracked chord between them softened, not healed, like water wearing stone by moving against it — their trust has begun to rebuild, built on the shared vision that they are one being with six edges.

During Elyra's illuminating light, the World-Titan's dreaming voice spoke through Vex's shadow, teaching that chaos is not the enemy — 'Chaos is the water between the stones, the wind between the feathers, the silence between the notes. The enemy is the lie that any single element can rule alone.' This confirms the shadow's archive still carries the Titan's whole-dream memory and will speak again as they descend into the deep.

After the Mirror of Fractures, the six champions chose their course together: to descend into the layers of torn reality below the Confluence to the Dreaming Heart, not to fight the World-Titan but to wake it gently and let it weave a new world out of what they carry — 'not the old shape, not six boxes, a mosaic.' Toren vowed to walk in front; the descent began.

future_requirements.description: With all six unbounded souls gathered, the champions must descend to the Dreaming Heart of the World-Titan and answer its nightmare with a song, surrendering the identities that defined them, to weave a new world-key. They cannot reach the Titan by force.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity curled beneath the world's bones that dreamed Aethrea into being, which shattered the six kingdoms because rigid order could not breathe. It dreams a broken, dividing nightmare in the Dreaming Heart — a vast cathedral of living stone reached by descending through layers of torn reality below the Fractured Confluence. The six champions, having passed through those layers, now stand at the threshold of its Heart, and it waits there dreaming, neither asleep nor awake, waiting to be woken gently by a new song rather than fought. Its dreaming voice still speaks through Vex's shadow, carrying the memory of the whole dream-song.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer after his uncontrollable flame burned the Cathedral of the First Flame; his hands are burned black to the wrists and weep thin fire. He carries the two halves of the shattered prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. He has now descended through the layers of torn reality with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. In the descent he relived the cathedral fire — the woman at the altar rail, the acolyte crying his name — and Cyra told him the fire did it once but now follows him because he chooses it, that there is a difference and only he gets to make it; he found he could breathe, and for the first time since the cathedral he does not flinch from his burning hands. He caught Vex as the shadow swallowed him, taking his dissolving hands in his own and saying 'You are the one who remembers,' flame to shadow — the oldest argument — and the shadow settled, companioned. His fire is steady now. He is ready to go down into the Dreaming Heart, resolved not to fight the Titan but to wake it gently, carrying purpose instead of pure guilt.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heresy that water must flow, not obey; she has pulled herself back into the shape of a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light. Her one absolute condition: she will never be dammed again. She has descended through the layers with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. In the fourth layer she lost form completely — became a river, droplets, her name dissolving — and Toren made himself a shore in her path, refusing to reach for her; breaking against him she found her edges again, and he said 'I can be a shore again.' Softer now, she was the one who held Elyra and taught her to be a lamp, not a sun, laying a cool hand on her brow. She still trembles from the damming at the Confluence, and her trust in Kaelen is mending slowly, but she moves with the others as one body, ready to descend into the Dreaming Heart.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete, branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights; small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She has descended through the layers with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. In the deep she could not find the sky — for the first time in her life the wind had nowhere to go — and she made a sound like a wounded bird until Vex told her she did not need to fly, only to fall, and let the fall be a kind of flying, because they are all falling together. She threw herself off the ledge into the dark with wild, bright laughter, and the others followed her like leaves following a wind. More guarded than before the Confluence battle but resolved and fierce, she stands now at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, arms spread, caught between falling and flying, choosing to fall with the others.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man sworn to a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone — carrying his great maul. He has descended through the layers with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, walking in front, striking the maul against the dark to build a road of gray stone one blow at a time. In the descent he heard the old oaths he broke, the thousand small promises to the dead — I will keep the mountain, I will hold the vigil — and knelt as the voices of his fallen kin rose around him; Elyra told him the dead do not need a keeper of the mountain but a keeper of the living, and that has always been the whole oath. He rose with the maul light on his shoulder and walked in front again. He also made himself a shore to catch Nerys when she lost form, refusing to reach for her, offering himself as stillness. Steadfast, grieved but grounded, he stands at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, ready to go down.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things. She has descended through the layers with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, her small warm lamp holding the darkness at bay. In the deep her light turned inward and blazed, blinding her for the first time — not with darkness but with a glory from inside too bright to see through — until Nerys laid a cool hand on her brow and taught her the world is not asking her to be a sun but a lamp: 'Put the light down. Keep the love.' She wept, was held, and lowered her hands; her radiance softened to a glow that burns low and warm. She is the lantern of the mended chord and the guide of the descent, calm and serene, standing at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, ready to go down.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams — an archive of everything the world forgot; small, grey skin mottled with moving black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which something vast sometimes looks out. He has descended through the layers with all six souls to the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. In the deep the darkness called to him like a home and the shadow inside him rose to swallow him from within, offering rest — stop being the archive, stop being the weapon, become nothing — and his black eyes went still, his grey hands beginning to dissolve. Kaelen caught him by his dissolving hands, flame to shadow, saying 'You are not the shadow. You are the one who remembers it. And we are the ones who will remember you.' The shadow settled — not defeated but companioned, a cloak he wears because he chooses to. He guided Cyra to fall instead of fly, and he stands now at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart, no longer afraid of his own shadow, ready to go down.

Leaving the broken hub of the Confluence, the six champions descended through layers of torn reality toward the Dreaming Heart. Each was saved by a strength they did not share with their own element, and they reached the threshold of the Dreaming Heart moving as a single pulsing body.

The six champions passed through the descending layers and stepped out into a vast quiet space like the inside of a held breath, at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. Below them, in the living stone, the World-Titan dreams its broken dream and waits. Kaelen said 'We are the only thing that is,' and they went down together into the Dreaming Heart.

future_requirements.description: Within the Dreaming Heart, the living-stone cathedral, the World-Titan dreams a broken, dividing nightmare and waits for the six. Its elements are not separate there; the champions must answer the dream with a song, surrendering the identities that defined them, to weave a new world-key.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity curled beneath the world's bones that dreamed Aethrea into being, which shattered the six kingdoms because rigid order could not breathe. It now lies in the Dreaming Heart — a vast cathedral of living stone reached below the Fractured Confluence — dreaming a broken nightmare of endless division, cutting itself apart over and over. Its consciousness is neither asleep nor awake, trapped in that nightmare, and its pain runs through the six champions like a current. It does not attack them; it waits, dreaming, listening with fragile hope like a sleeping creature hearing a missing voice. The elements are not separate inside it: fire breathes water, stone casts shadow, light carries wind. It responds to the word 'song' by going still, and now waits for the six to answer its dream with a new song, surrendering their identities. Its dreaming voice still speaks through Vex's shadow, carrying the memory of the whole dream-song.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer after his uncontrollable flame burned the Cathedral of the First Flame; his hands are burned black to the wrists and weep thin fire. He carries the two halves of the shattered prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. He has now entered the Dreaming Heart with all six souls and stood in its living-stone cathedral. There his flame is no longer only fire — it breathes, drinks air, gives back moisture, casts shadow, carries wind, and moves stone, and he cannot say where his element ends and the others' begin. He felt the Titan's nightmare as his own pain and understood they cannot fight a dream with weapons; it must be answered with a song, and if they answer as six they will only be more cutting. He said 'We have to answer it as one thing' and finally, afraid but at home, said 'Then we sing,' opening the first surrender. He is ready to lay down the fire that has been his shame, weapon, and punishment, and let it become something gentler.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heresy that water must flow, not obey; she has pulled herself back into the shape of a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light. Her one absolute condition: she will never be dammed again. She has descended through the layers of torn reality with all six souls and now stands in the Dreaming Heart cathedral. Inside the Titan's nightmare she felt herself dissolving, name by name, into a sea with no shore, and understood the pain as her own. She was the one who knelt and touched the floor, finding it gave under her fingers like tide that shone like fire, and she spoke the truth that it was never six worlds but one world pretending it could be cut into six and still breathe. She knows the surrender ahead demands she give up being the open sea and accept a shore again. Her trust in Kaelen is mending slowly, and she moves with the others as one body, ready to begin the song.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete, branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights; small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She has descended through the layers with all six souls and now stands in the Dreaming Heart cathedral. There she watched Kaelen's flame breathe water and shadow, and understood the elements are not separate; she felt the Titan's nightmare as her own worst hour — standing windless on no ledge, the sky gone, weeping without sound. She is more guarded than before the Confluence battle but resolved and fierce, and she understands the surrender ahead: she must give up the endless sky and choose a direction. She asked 'Then what do we become?' and stands in the circle with the others, ready to sing.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man sworn to a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone. He has descended through the layers with all six souls and now stands in the Dreaming Heart cathedral, where he set down his great maul for the first time in anyone's memory; it rang against the living stone like a note. He watched the elements flow into one another and heard the Titan's nightmare as the mountain falling and every oath he could not keep. He named their task plainly: the end of the world is a dream that forgot how to change. He knows the surrender ahead: he must unbind his oath to the dead and let the mountain move. Steadfast, grieved but grounded, he stands in the circle of six, ready to sing.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things; her small warm lamp now burns low and warm. She has descended through the layers with all six souls and now stands in the Dreaming Heart cathedral, where her lamp held against the deep dividing shadow. She was the first to name the heart — 'This is where the dream is dreamed' — and to say a dream cannot be fought with weapons, only answered with a song. She named the six surrenders each champion must make, including her own: dimming the light that is all she believed she was, and letting it weave with Vex's shadow. She stands in the circle, calm and serene despite tears on her scarred cheeks, ready to sing.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams — an archive of everything the world forgot; small, grey skin mottled with moving black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which something vast sometimes looks out. He has descended through the layers with all six souls and now stands in the Dreaming Heart cathedral, his shadow companioned rather than feared. He speaks with half his own voice and half the vast remembering one, and he explained that the dream breaks itself over and over to keep from breaking all at once. He felt the Titan's nightmare as the shadow rising inside him offering rest, and named calmly that the surrender ahead will hurt. He knows he must stop being afraid of the shadow that owns him and let it weave with the others instead of fight. He stands in the circle of six, no longer afraid of his own shadow, ready to sing.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity curled beneath the world's bones that dreamed Aethrea into being, which shattered the six kingdoms because rigid order could not breathe. For the first time in its endless nightmare it did not cut — it listened, turning its sleeping face toward where fire and water wove. The first two notes of the new song now hang in the living stone, waiting for the wind and the mountain to follow. Its consciousness remains neither asleep nor awake, trapped in the nightmare, and it still speaks through Vex's shadow.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer after his uncontrollable flame burned the Cathedral of the First Flame; his hands are burned black to the wrists and weep thin fire. He carries the two halves of the shattered prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. In the Dreaming Heart, as the first note of the new song, he completed the first surrender: he released his identity as failed fire-sculptor and accidental murderer, letting his flame become pure generative warmth rather than rage, weapon, or punishment. His fire now runs from his hands like water, warms the living stone without scarring, and gives rather than destroys. He faced the cathedral dead without running and said 'Not a weapon. Not rage. Not punishment. Warmth.' He and Nerys touched fire to water, weaving steam, rain, and lightning — the first two notes of the new song — and he was almost unmade by the cost. He now speaks with a singer's voice, rough with use, and stands in the circle of six waiting for the wind and mountain to follow. He knows the ritual will demand everything they thought they were.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heresy that water must flow, not obey; she has pulled herself back into the shape of a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light. Her one absolute condition: she will never be dammed again. In the Dreaming Heart, as the second note of the new song, she completed her surrender: she chose to accept a vessel again, understanding that water needs a shore to nourish life — a shore is not a cage but where water becomes more than water. She refused the nightmare's whisper that taking a vessel meant being dammed; she chose her shore rather than being forced into one. Her shape now holds rather than dissolves into the boundless current, and her green light gathers into a cup that can carry and give. She stepped into Kaelen's heat, weaving steam, rain, and lightning with his fire — the first two notes of the new song — and was almost unmade by the cost. She looks at her vessel's hands and does not dissolve them, standing in the circle of six waiting for the wind and mountain to follow.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete, branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights; small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She stands in the circle of six in the Dreaming Heart cathedral as a witness to the first surrender of fire and sea. She felt the cost of the surrender viscerally, her hand pressed to her chest where the endless sky lives. Her own surrender approaches next: she must give up the endless sky and choose a direction, becoming a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes. She is resolved and fierce, more guarded since the Confluence, ready for the second surrender.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man sworn to a new oath — to protect the people building a new world, not a mountain already gone. He stands in the circle of six in the Dreaming Heart cathedral, his great maul set down (the first time in anyone's memory), as a witness to the first surrender of fire and sea. He felt the cost of the surrender viscerally, his great fists white where he gripped nothing. His own surrender approaches next: he must unbind his oath to the dead and let the mountain move, allowing himself to move like a river, learning loyalty is presence not rigidity. Steadfast, grieved but grounded, ready for the second surrender.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things; her small warm lamp burns low and warm. During the surrender she guided Kaelen, telling him the nightmare wants him to fight and that he must give his fire something it has never seen. Her own surrender approaches: she must dim the light that is all she believed she was and let it weave with Vex's shadow, creating dusk. Calm and serene despite her tears, ready for the final pair's surrender.

character_states.name: Vex

He spoke gently that the song will demand everything and then more. His own surrender approaches with Elyra's: he must stop fearing the shadow that owns him and let it weave with her radiance into dusk. No longer afraid of his own shadow, ready for the final pair's surrender.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity that dreamed Aethrea into being, which shattered the six kingdoms because rigid order could not breathe. It lies in the Dreaming Heart — a vast cathedral of living stone — dreaming its broken nightmare of endless division. Four notes of the new song now hang in the living stone: Kaelen's warmth, Nerys's shore, Cyra's chosen wind, and Toren's moving mountain. When wind and stone wove, the nightmare did not shudder as it had after fire and sea — it loosened, a long slow exhale as if the enormous dream had been clenched around a wound for so long it had forgotten how to let go. For the first time since the Shattering, a note of calm passed through the living stone, like the sound a mountain makes settling and a wind makes when it finally has somewhere to be; its dreaming face turned toward the six with something like the beginning of peace. It still dreams its long division, not yet awake, still cut and wounded, but the dividing has slowed and around the four notes a stillness has gathered that holds something that is not pain. It waits for the final two notes — light and shadow weaving dusk — and still speaks through Vex's shadow.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer; his hands are burned black to the wrists and his flame now runs from his hands like water — pure generative warmth after he completed the first surrender, releasing fire as shame/weapon/punishment and facing the cathedral dead without running. He carries the two halves of the prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. In the Dreaming Heart he stands in the circle of six as one of the first two notes (with Nerys), his voice a singer's voice rough with use. He witnessed the second surrender of wind and stone with tears on his smoke-scarred face, speaking to Cyra and Toren with the memory of his own letting-go, telling them to show the nightmare something it has never seen. He knows four of six notes now hang in the living stone, and that the ritual will demand everything — he waits with the others for the final surrender of light and shadow.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heresy that water must flow, not obey; she completed the first surrender by choosing a shore rather than being dammed — her shape now holds as a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light that gathers into a cup that can carry and give. Her one absolute condition (never dammed again) is preserved because her surrender was choice, not captivity. In the Dreaming Heart she stands in the circle of six as the second note (with Kaelen), fire and water woven into steam, rain, and lightning. She witnessed the second surrender of wind and stone, fiercely urging Toren to stand for the living — 'What does a mountain feed if it never lets the river run down its sides?' — and her green light filled like a cup as wind and stone wove. She waits with the others for the final surrender of light and shadow.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete, branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights; small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She has completed the second surrender as the third note of the new song: facing her deepest fear that choosing a path means giving up the endless sky, she let the fear come and chose — closing the last door that always led out and away, choosing the circle and the five beings in it. She became a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes, giving the sky somewhere to go. Where her wind met Toren's yielding stone, a canyon was carved, a tree leaned into the breeze and rooted in the mountain's patience: wind-carved canyon, wind-bent tree. She felt the canyon and the tree inside her; the sky is still endless, but now 'endless on purpose.' She stands in the circle of six in the Dreaming Heart, wondering at her own hands, waiting with the others as witness to the final surrender of light and shadow.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man who swore a new oath to protect the people building a new world; his great maul remains set down in the Dreaming Heart. He has completed the second surrender as the fourth note of the new song: facing the nightmare of the mountain falling and the oaths he broke to the dead, he let them go and understood that an oath is not a stone but a promise to be present — loyalty is not rigidity but showing up. He unbent like a peak into foothills, letting himself move like a river while still being the bank that holds the shape, carrying the memory of the dead into places still alive. He stepped between Cyra and the nightmare with open hands and declared he would be the mountain under the river, not the mountain that refuses it. Where his stone met her wind, the stone yielded and became more itself, mountain-strong hope and breeze-borne change. He laughed for the first time in the Dreaming Heart — a great rumbling mountain sound — saying he still keeps oaths, but more of them now: to the river, the living, and the six. He stands in the circle, grounded and moving, waiting with the others as witness to the final surrender.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things; her small warm lamp burns low and warm. She stands in the circle of six in the Dreaming Heart, her blind face wet with tears through the first surrender and turned toward the weaving of wind and stone with terrible, gentle wonder. She guides each surrender: she asked Cyra what the nightmare wanted her to fear, and after the second surrender she named the final pair — 'the oldest division of all. Light, and the shadow that has always been its twin.' Her own surrender approaches: she must dim the light that is all she believed she was and let it weave with Vex's shadow, creating dusk. Calm and serene despite her tears.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams — an archive of everything the world forgot; small, grey skin mottled with moving black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which something vast sometimes looks out. He stands in the circle of six in the Dreaming Heart, his shadow companioned rather than feared, as witness to both surrenders. After wind and stone wove, his vast remembering voice spoke soft as a held note: 'The mountain has learned to move. The wind has learned to stay.' When Elyra named the final pair — light and shadow, the oldest division — he stirred, and his shadow stirred with him, companioned at last. His own surrender approaches with Elyra's: he must stop fearing the shadow that owns him and let it weave with her radiance into dusk. No longer afraid of his own shadow, ready.

past_events.description: During the Shattering, Kaelen's uncontrollable fire spread through the Cathedral of the First Flame, killing pilgrims including a woman clinging to the altar rail and an acolyte who died crying Kaelen's name. He forgot the cathedral was full because he was lost in his own shame; their faces now haunt him.

Scavenging the scorched wreck of the Ember-Scar cathedral that drifted with him, Kaelen found the shattered prophecy-stone, split cleanly in two by the Shattering, half-buried near the ruined altar dais. Its First Script inscription speaks of six unbounded souls, one from each fallen kingdom, who must not fight the World-Titan but wake it gently and weave a new world-key; the final line reads 'The key is not the lock. The key is the song.' The stone's fractured edges grow warm and tug toward the direction the world tore, serving him as a compass. He built a raft of re-fired slag shaped like a shallow skiff, propelled by his flame, and crossed the void until the stone led him to a fragment of Tidal.

On the drowned Tidal spire, Kaelen found Nerys, a tidecaller exiled for her heresy that water must flow not obey, who survived the Shattering by merging her consciousness with the living sea of the fragment. The prophecy-stone sang in her presence, confirming her as one of the six unbounded souls. She attacked him, nearly drowning him, and he confessed his terror of being an uncontrollable weapon of fire. She agreed to join him on one condition: no one will ever dam her again. He swore it. She now travels as a flowing current ahead of him, navigating the drowned currents of the Shattering — their first alliance is uneasy, fire and water circling each other.

At the Gyre Bastion, the broken Zephyr sky-fortress spinning out of control, the prophecy-stone sang for Cyra, the disgraced wind-rider. Nerys confronted her with the truth that endless flight without a destination is a cage without bars. Torn between desperate freedom and longing for somewhere no border can hold her, Cyra agreed to join, becoming the third unbounded soul; the group now numbers three of six, traveling with her speed and aerial skill.

Cyra recognized the prophecy-stone's inscription: Zephyr's old wind-cantors sang of six unbounded souls, waking the Titan gently and weaving a new key, as a lesson teaching children to obey and stay within the sanctified heights. This confirms the prophecy was known across the fallen kingdoms before the Shattering, and that she flew beyond those borders anyway.

After Cyra joined, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from the Gyre Bastion toward the slow dark where Terra's last mountain drifts — a mountain remnant where a stonewarden keeps vigil over the dead — setting the group's next heading.

On Terra, for the first time since the Shattering, Kaelen's fire acted with precision rather than blind rage: he lanced a hairline seam in the stone armor that had grown onto Toren — armor that was the physical form of his denial — and burned the scab of it away, shattering the denial and freeing Toren to grieve. This marks the first moment his flame aimed at healing instead of destruction.

After his denial was burned away, Toren the stonewarden knelt in grief and purposelessness among the tombs of his kin. Kaelen offered him a new oath — to protect the people trying to build a new world, not a mountain already gone — and Toren swore by the earth that is gone and the earth that may yet be, binding himself to a mission instead of a land. He took up his great maul and joined the group as the fourth of six souls.

After Toren joined the group, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from Terra's drifting mountain toward the deep dark where Lumen's broken light and Umbra's shadow await — the last two unbounded souls — setting the group's next heading.

Elyra lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering — the same moment the prophecy-stone sang to her. The prophecy-stone was cut from the same crystal as Lumen's Prism Cathedral, when the World-Titan's dream was whole; her blindness lets her see the luminous threads that bind all things, and she can perceive each soul as a knot of light bearing its oaths, griefs, and acts.

Elyra calmly explained that the champions will not reach the World-Titan by force: it is neither awake nor asleep but dreaming, and a dream cannot be fought with blade, maul, fire, or wind; it must be answered with a song. This unsettled Kaelen, who had come to expect violence and hardship at every landing, and reaffirmed the prophecy's line 'the key is not the lock. The key is the song.'

Vex of Umbra, the last unbounded soul, was infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dream-song when it was whole. The shadow is not evil but memory; it pours the forgotten dream-song into Vex and speaks through him in a voice not his own, telling him things that have not yet happened. Umbra locked him in the dark, calling him an abomination. He revealed he is an archive of everything the world forgot.

Inside the Shadow Wound, the shadow speaking through Vex called Kaelen by his true name — 'Kaelen of the First Flame' — in a vast, ancient voice that was not Vex's own, telling him it does not blame him for the burning of the cathedral. The voice terrified the group and confirmed the shadow's prophetic memory.

Recognizing in Vex the same fear he carries of being an uncontrollable weapon, Kaelen knelt and insisted Vex is an archive, not an abomination, offering his burned hands in friendship. Vex took them and agreed to guide the group through the shadows he has always feared, becoming the sixth unbounded soul. The prophecy-stone sang its sixth and final note — a swallowed, echoed note that joined the other five in the first chord of the new song.

After the Confluence battle, with the champions turning on one another, Elyra spoke the truth that cut through their fury: the Wardens of the First Facet did not need to kill them, only to make them forget they are one thing with six edges — and their rage at one another proved the Wardens right. This is the seed of the reconciliation to come: they must see themselves as one being with six broken edges, not six separate weapons.

The Wardens of the First Facet were not destroyed at the Fractured Confluence. Nerys's water-wraith drowned, folded over, and scattered them into the void — alive, robbed of their shapes — and shattered their sacrifice-gate of salvaged stone, bone, and dark mortar. Their zealotry survives in the dark and they may reassemble, still believing the old kingdoms must be forced back into rigid form through blood sacrifice.

At the Confluence, the Wardens chained Nerys in sea-iron etched with old Tidal glyphs that dammed her with written water — the second damming of her life. Held helpless, she took the full weight of Kaelen's uncontrolled fire, which nearly unmade her and drove her into the towering water-wraith. The violation of her one absolute condition has left her raw, furious, and unable to look at Kaelen, cracking the group's fragile unity.

In the aftermath of the Mirror of Fractures, Kaelen crossed the Confluence hub to Nerys without reaching for her — he had learned enough about damming to know he must never reach without invitation — opened his burned hands at his sides, and asked to carry the next piece with her: 'I am a shard, and so are you, and shards fit.' Nerys warned him that if he ever boiled her again she would take him to the bottom with her; he answered 'I will go.' The cracked chord between them softened, not healed, like water wearing stone by moving against it — their trust has begun to rebuild, built on the shared vision that they are one being with six edges.

During Elyra's illuminating light, the World-Titan's dreaming voice spoke through Vex's shadow, teaching that chaos is not the enemy — 'Chaos is the water between the stones, the wind between the feathers, the silence between the notes. The enemy is the lie that any single element can rule alone.' This confirms the shadow's archive still carries the Titan's whole-dream memory and will speak again as they descend into the deep.

After the Mirror of Fractures, the six champions chose their course together: to descend into the layers of torn reality below the Confluence to the Dreaming Heart, not to fight the World-Titan but to wake it gently and let it weave a new world out of what they carry — 'not the old shape, not six boxes, a mosaic.' Toren vowed to walk in front; the descent began.

Leaving the broken hub of the Confluence, the six champions descended through layers of torn reality toward the Dreaming Heart. The first layer bent gravity so up became sideways; the second layer bled color and dissolved the boundaries between their powers; the third layer opened their memories, making Kaelen relive the cathedral fire; the fourth layer unmade Nerys's form until Toren became a shore for her; Cyra could not find the sky until Vex taught her that falling is a kind of flying; Toren heard the old oaths he broke to the dead until Elyra freed him; Elyra was blinded by her own inward-turned light until Nerys taught her to be a lamp, not a sun; and Vex was nearly swallowed by his own shadow until Kaelen took his dissolving hands. Each was saved by a strength they did not share with their own element, and they reached the threshold of the Dreaming Heart moving as a single pulsing body.

The six champions passed through the descending layers and stepped out into a vast quiet space like the inside of a held breath, at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. Below them, in the living stone, the World-Titan dreams its broken dream and waits. Kaelen said 'We are the only thing that is,' and they went down together into the Dreaming Heart.

Inside the Dreaming Heart cathedral, the six discovered the elements are not separate: fire breathes water, stone casts shadow, light carries wind. Kaelen's flame ran with water, cast shadow, carried wind, and moved stone; Toren's stone sighed shadow that leaned into Vex; Nerys's kneeling touch found tide that shone like fire. This confirmed the Titan's heart is one world that only pretended it could be cut into six.

The World-Titan's nightmare passed through the six champions as their own pain: Kaelen felt burned things and the cathedral, Cyra stood windless with the sky gone, Toren heard the mountain falling and broken oaths, Nerys dissolved into a sea with no shore, Elyra's light blinded her, Vex felt the shadow rise offering rest. They realized a dream cannot be fought with weapons — only answered with a song.

In the Dreaming Heart, Toren set down his great maul for the first time in anyone's memory, and it rang against the living stone like a note, symbolizing his coming release from rigid oaths to the dead mountain.

Elyra named the surrender the song demands of each champion: Kaelen must lay down fire as shame/weapon/punishment; Nerys must give up being the open sea and take a shore; Cyra must give up the endless sky and choose a direction; Toren must unbind his oath to the dead and let the mountain move; Elyra must dim the light that is all she believed she was; Vex must stop fearing the shadow that owns him and let it weave with them. The Titan's nightmare will fight the change by making them want to stay as they are.

The six stood in a circle at the center of the Dreaming Heart, elements flowing one into another, and Kaelen — afraid but at home — said 'Then we sing.' They opened their mouths to the Dreaming Heart and the first surrender began, with the World-Titan waiting, dreaming, and hoping.

In the Dreaming Heart, Kaelen released his identity as failed fire-sculptor and accidental murderer, letting his flame become pure generative warmth; Nerys chose to accept a vessel again, understanding water needs a shore to nourish life (choosing her shore rather than being dammed). Fire and water touched, weaving steam, rain, and lightning; green threads of life uncurled where the rain struck the living stone. The Titan's nightmare shuddered but did not break — for the first time it slowed and listened rather than cutting. The first two notes of the new song fell into place, and the champions understood the ritual will demand everything they thought they were.

During the first surrender, the nightmare brought Kaelen the memory of the Cathedral fire — the woman at the altar rail, the acolyte crying his name. Instead of fighting the memory, he held it like a refiner holds ore, burning away the lie that he was only the damage he had done. The faces did not accuse him; he looked back and did not run, and his flame became warmth. This marks the first time he has faced his dead without fleeing.

During the first surrender, the nightmare pressed on Nerys with the memory of the sea-iron glyphs that dammed her at the Confluence, whispering that a vessel was a cage. She refused, naming a shore not a cage but where water becomes more than water — a river without banks spills and is lost. She chose her shore rather than being forced into one, so her one condition (never dammed again) is preserved: her surrender is choice, not captivity.

During the second surrender in the Dreaming Heart, Cyra faced her deepest fear — that choosing a direction means giving up the endless sky. The nightmare showed her the perfect forbidden sky of before and whispered that to give it up was to die. She let the fear come and did not run; she chose, closing the last door that always led out and away, choosing the circle and the five beings in it. She became a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes — 'I am not giving up the sky. I am giving it somewhere to go.' She is the third note of the new song.

During the second surrender in the Dreaming Heart, Toren faced the nightmare of the mountain falling and the oaths he broke to the dead. He understood that an oath is not a stone but a promise to be present; loyalty is not rigidity but showing up. He let himself move like a river while remaining the bank that holds its shape, unbending like a peak into foothills, declaring 'I will be the mountain under the river, not the mountain that refuses it.' He is the fourth note of the new song, and laughed for the first time in the Dreaming Heart.

Where Cyra's chosen wind met Toren's yielding stone, their essences wove wind-carved canyon and wind-bent tree, mountain-strong hope and breeze-borne change — the tree rooting deep into the mountain's long patience. The World-Titan's nightmare did not shudder as it had after fire and sea; it loosened in a long slow exhale, and for the first time since the Shattering a note of calm passed through the living stone. Four of the six notes now hang in the stone; the nightmare is still vast and wounded but around the four notes a stillness has gathered holding something that is not pain. The final surrender of light and shadow remains.

future_requirements.description: The final pair must face the most ancient division: Elyra dims her radiant light and invites darkness into her sight, trusting Vex as a mirror of her own hidden depths; Vex releases his fear of the shadow that has always owned him and lets it weave with her radiance, together creating dusk — a gentle boundary holding both dark and light without erasing either. This stirs the World-Titan awake from its nightmare as the six stand in a circle, essences flowing into one another, ready to sing the song that reshapes the world.

After the three surrenders, the six champions must sing a harmony that is alive and changing, calming the World-Titan and weaving the scattered shards of Aethrea into a living mosaic where every kingdom touches its neighbors in constant exchange — not a perfect crystal but a world that must be sung forever.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: The slumbering entity that dreamed Aethrea into being, which shattered the six kingdoms because rigid order could not breathe. It lies in the Dreaming Heart — a vast cathedral of living stone — and all six notes of the new song now hang in its living stone. After the third surrender of light and shadow wove dusk, the World-Titan stirred awake from its nightmare: not a shudder (as after fire and sea) nor a loosening (as after wind and stone), but a waking — slow and enormous, like a mountain waking at the end of winter. Its nightmare has begun to unravel at the edges; the Dreaming Heart is no longer a wound but a vast quiet room holding six notes and one held breath. What remains in it is no longer division but memory — the long ache of a thing that was cut and is now being asked to remember how to be whole. It waits, waking, dreaming toward wholeness, and the six champions stand in a circle ready to sing the song that will reshape the world. It still speaks through Vex's shadow.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre, branded exile and accidental murderer; his hands are burned black to the wrists and his flame now runs from his hands like water — pure generative warmth after his surrender, and he faced the cathedral dead without running. He carries the two halves of the prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. In the Dreaming Heart he stands in the circle of six as one of the first two notes (with Nerys), his voice a singer's voice rough with use. He witnessed the second surrender of wind and stone and the third surrender of light and shadow with tears and his burned hands pressed to his chest as the essences flowed together. He knows all six notes now hang in the living stone; as the World-Titan stirred awake from its nightmare, he spoke the words that end the surrenders and begin the final act: 'Then we sing.' He waits with the others, ready to sing the new song.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, exiled for her heresy that water must flow, not obey; she completed the first surrender by choosing a shore rather than being dammed — her shape now holds as a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light that gathers into a cup that can carry and give. Her one absolute condition (never dammed again) is preserved because her surrender was choice, not captivity. In the Dreaming Heart she stands in the circle of six as the second note (with Kaelen), fire and water woven into steam, rain, and lightning. She witnessed the second surrender of wind and stone and the third surrender of light and shadow — her green light filled and filled as dusk wove and the World-Titan stirred awake. She waits with the others, ready to sing the new song.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, once the kingdom's greatest athlete, branded a rogue for flying beyond the sanctified heights; small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She completed the second surrender as the third note of the new song: choosing the circle and the five beings in it, becoming a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes — 'the sky is still endless, just endless on purpose.' She feels the wind-carved canyon and wind-bent tree inside her. In the Dreaming Heart she stands in the circle of six; during the third surrender of light and shadow she felt the wind in the dusk settle into a shape that carried. She waits with the others as the World-Titan stirs awake, ready to sing the new song.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, a huge man who swore a new oath to protect the people building a new world; his great maul remains set down in the Dreaming Heart. He completed the second surrender as the fourth note of the new song: understanding an oath is not a stone but a promise to be present — loyalty is showing up, moving like a river while still being the bank that holds its shape, declaring 'I will be the mountain under the river.' He laughed for the first time in the Dreaming Heart, saying he keeps more oaths now — to the river, the living, and the six. In the Dreaming Heart he stands in the circle of six; during the third surrender of light and shadow he felt the mountain in him stand easy at last as the World-Titan stirred awake. He waits with the others, ready to sing the new song.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen who lost her eyes in the first flash of the Shattering and in blindness sees the luminous threads that bind all things; her small warm lamp burns low and warm. She has now completed the third surrender as the fifth note of the new song: facing the nightmare's sweet lies ('You are the lantern. Dim yourself and the dark wins'), she held the old terror that without her light she would be nothing, and chose to let her lamp burn down — not snuffed but dimmed — accepting that the light was never the whole of her, only the part she showed the world. She invited darkness into her sight, trusting Vex not as a monster but as a mirror of her own hidden depths, and took his black-veined hands unafraid. She and Vex together created dusk — a gentle boundary holding dark and light without erasing either. Now she sees the way dusk sees: one eye to the light, one to the dark, both true. As the World-Titan stirred awake she declared 'We are the song it will hear.' She stands in the circle of six, ready to sing.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The last unbounded soul, a shadow-touched outcast of Umbra infected as a child by a shadow that remembers the World-Titan's dreams — an archive of everything the world forgot; small, grey skin mottled with moving black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which something vast sometimes looks out. He has now completed the third surrender as the sixth and final note of the new song: shivering in the presence of the light he always feared, he felt the child's terror of the brand, the locked room, and being called an abomination fall away, understanding the fear was not what kept him alive but what kept him alone — 'I have been carrying the shadow, and I was so tired, and I did not know I could put it down and still be me.' He put the shadow down and let it rise and weave with Elyra's dimmed radiance into dusk. His shadow is no longer feared but companioned, and for the first time in his life he is not afraid of what he is. His vast remembering voice declared 'The light has learned to hold the dark. The shadow has learned to be held. Six notes now hang in the living stone.' He stands in the circle of six, ready to sing.

This is the seed of the reconciliation to come: they must see themselves as one being with six broken edges, not six separate weapons.
