Nerys's water-wraith drowned, folded over, and scattered them into the void — alive, robbed of their shapes — and shattered their sacrifice-gate of salvaged stone, bone, and dark mortar. Their zealotry survives in the dark and they may reassemble, still believing the old kingdoms must be forced back into rigid form through blood sacrifice.

At the Confluence, the Wardens chained Nerys in sea-iron etched with old Tidal glyphs that dammed her with written water — the second damming of her life. Held helpless, she took the full weight of Kaelen's uncontrolled fire, which nearly unmade her and drove her into the towering water-wraith. The violation of her one absolute condition has left her raw, furious, and unable to look at Kaelen, cracking the group's fragile unity.

In the aftermath of the Mirror of Fractures, Kaelen crossed the Confluence hub to Nerys without reaching for her — he had learned enough about damming to know he must never reach without invitation — opened his burned hands at his sides, and asked to carry the next piece with her: 'I am a shard, and so are you, and shards fit.' Nerys warned him that if he ever boiled her again she would take him to the bottom with her; he answered 'I will go.' The cracked chord between them softened, not healed, like water wearing stone by moving against it — their trust has begun to rebuild, built on the shared vision that they are one being with six edges.

During Elyra's illuminating light, the World-Titan's dreaming voice spoke through Vex's shadow, teaching that chaos is not the enemy — 'Chaos is the water between the stones, the wind between the feathers, the silence between the notes. The enemy is the lie that any single element can rule alone.' This confirms the shadow's archive still carries the Titan's whole-dream memory and will speak again as they descend into the deep.

After the Mirror of Fractures, the six champions chose their course together: to descend into the layers of torn reality below the Confluence to the Dreaming Heart, not to fight the World-Titan but to wake it gently and let it weave a new world out of what they carry — 'not the old shape, not six boxes, a mosaic.' Toren vowed to walk in front; the descent began.

Leaving the broken hub of the Confluence, the six champions descended through layers of torn reality toward the Dreaming Heart. The first layer bent gravity so up became sideways; the second layer bled color and dissolved the boundaries between their powers; the third layer opened their memories, making Kaelen relive the cathedral fire; the fourth layer unmade Nerys's form until Toren became a shore for her; Cyra could not find the sky until Vex taught her that falling is a kind of flying; Toren heard the old oaths he broke to the dead until Elyra freed him; Elyra was blinded by her own inward-turned light until Nerys taught her to be a lamp, not a sun; and Vex was nearly swallowed by his own shadow until Kaelen took his dissolving hands. Each was saved by a strength they did not share with their own element, and they reached the threshold of the Dreaming Heart moving as a single pulsing body.

The six champions passed through the descending layers and stepped out into a vast quiet space like the inside of a held breath, at the threshold of the Dreaming Heart. Below them, in the living stone, the World-Titan dreams its broken dream and waits. Kaelen said 'We are the only thing that is,' and they went down together into the Dreaming Heart.

Inside the Dreaming Heart cathedral, the six discovered the elements are not separate: fire breathes water, stone casts shadow, light carries wind. Kaelen's flame ran with water, cast shadow, carried wind, and moved stone; Toren's stone sighed shadow that leaned into Vex; Nerys's kneeling touch found tide that shone like fire. This confirmed the Titan's heart is one world that only pretended it could be cut into six.

The World-Titan's nightmare passed through the six champions as their own pain: Kaelen felt burned things and the cathedral, Cyra stood windless with the sky gone, Toren heard the mountain falling and broken oaths, Nerys dissolved into a sea with no shore, Elyra's light blinded her, Vex felt the shadow rise offering rest. They realized a dream cannot be fought with weapons — only answered with a song.

In the Dreaming Heart, Toren set down his great maul for the first time in anyone's memory, and it rang against the living stone like a note, symbolizing his coming release from rigid oaths to the dead mountain.

Elyra named the surrender the song demands of each champion: Kaelen must lay down fire as shame/weapon/punishment; Nerys must give up being the open sea and take a shore; Cyra must give up the endless sky and choose a direction; Toren must unbind his oath to the dead and let the mountain move; Elyra must dim the light that is all she believed she was; Vex must stop fearing the shadow that owns him and let it weave with them. The Titan's nightmare will fight the change by making them want to stay as they are.

The six stood in a circle at the center of the Dreaming Heart, elements flowing one into another, and Kaelen — afraid but at home — said 'Then we sing.' They opened their mouths to the Dreaming Heart and the first surrender began, with the World-Titan waiting, dreaming, and hoping.

In the Dreaming Heart, Kaelen released his identity as failed fire-sculptor and accidental murderer, letting his flame become pure generative warmth; Nerys chose to accept a vessel again, understanding water needs a shore to nourish life (choosing her shore rather than being dammed). Fire and water touched, weaving steam, rain, and lightning; green threads of life uncurled where the rain struck the living stone. The Titan's nightmare shuddered but did not break — for the first time it slowed and listened rather than cutting. The first two notes of the new song fell into place, and the champions understood the ritual will demand everything they thought they were.

During the first surrender, the nightmare brought Kaelen the memory of the Cathedral fire — the woman at the altar rail, the acolyte crying his name. Instead of fighting the memory, he held it like a refiner holds ore, burning away the lie that he was only the damage he had done. The faces did not accuse him; he looked back and did not run, and his flame became warmth. This marks the first time he has faced his dead without fleeing.

During the first surrender, the nightmare pressed on Nerys with the memory of the sea-iron glyphs that dammed her at the Confluence, whispering that a vessel was a cage. She refused, naming a shore not a cage but where water becomes more than water — a river without banks spills and is lost. She chose her shore rather than being forced into one, so her one condition (never dammed again) is preserved: her surrender is choice, not captivity.

During the second surrender in the Dreaming Heart, Cyra faced her deepest fear — that choosing a direction means giving up the endless sky. The nightmare showed her the perfect forbidden sky of before and whispered that to give it up was to die. She let the fear come and did not run; she chose, closing the last door that always led out and away, choosing the circle and the five beings in it. She became a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes — 'I am not giving up the sky. I am giving it somewhere to go.' She is the third note of the new song.

During the second surrender in the Dreaming Heart, Toren faced the nightmare of the mountain falling and the oaths he broke to the dead. He understood that an oath is not a stone but a promise to be present; loyalty is not rigidity but showing up. He let himself move like a river while remaining the bank that holds its shape, unbending like a peak into foothills, declaring 'I will be the mountain under the river, not the mountain that refuses it.' He is the fourth note of the new song, and laughed for the first time in the Dreaming Heart.

Where Cyra's chosen wind met Toren's yielding stone, their essences wove wind-carved canyon and wind-bent tree, mountain-strong hope and breeze-borne change — the tree rooting deep into the mountain's long patience. The World-Titan's nightmare did not shudder as it had after fire and sea; it loosened in a long slow exhale, and for the first time since the Shattering a note of calm passed through the living stone. Four of the six notes now hang in the stone; the nightmare is still vast and wounded but around the four notes a stillness has gathered holding something that is not pain. The final surrender of light and shadow remains.

In the Dreaming Heart, Elyra and Vex completed the final surrender, weaving dusk. Elyra faced the nightmare's sweet lies and chose to let her lamp burn down (not snuffed but dimmed), accepting the light was never the whole of her; she invited darkness into her sight and took Vex's black-veined hands, trusting him as a mirror of her own hidden depths. Vex released the child's fear of the shadow that had owned him since Umbra, put the shadow down, and let it rise to weave with her radiance. Where they touched they created dusk — a gentle boundary holding both dark and light without erasing either — in which all six colors of Aethrea ran and none fought. The fifth and sixth notes of the new song now hang in the living stone.

Its nightmare began to unravel at the edges; the Dreaming Heart became a vast quiet room holding six notes and one held breath. What remained in it was no longer division but memory — the long ache of a thing that was cut being asked to remember how to be whole. It leans in to listen, ready for the new song.

As the World-Titan stirred awake, the six champions' essences flowed one into another around the circle: fire breathed water, stone cast shadow, light carried wind, and every element touched every other — six edges of one being fitting together at last like the shards of a gem remembering they were never six pieces but one song. Kaelen spoke 'Then we sing,' and the Dreaming Heart leaned in to listen, ready for the song that will reshape the world.

future_requirements.description: After the three surrenders, the six champions must sing a harmony that is alive and changing, calming the World-Titan and weaving the scattered shards of Aethrea into a living mosaic where every kingdom touches its neighbors in constant exchange — not a perfect crystal but a world that must be sung forever.

character_states.name: World-Titan
character_states.description: Fully awake at last, its nightmare unraveled and replaced by memory and wholeness. Its Dreaming Heart — the vast cathedral of living stone at the center of the new world — now holds the six notes of the new song as its own heartbeat. Through the song it wove the scattered shards of Aethrea into a living mosaic rather than a perfect crystal: fire sparks the seas, waters nourish the drifting mountains of Terra, winds scatter Lumen's light into Umbra's shadows, and every kingdom touches its neighbors in constant exchange. It dreams the new world awake, no longer divided, its long ache of being cut healed into the daily rhythm of dusk and dawn. It continues to speak through Vex's companioned shadow, but now gently.

character_states.name: Kaelen
character_states.description: A disgraced fire-sculptor of Pyre who became one of the six guardians of the new world. His hands remain burned black to the wrists, but for the first time they move with steadiness; he still carries the two halves of the prophecy-stone wrapped in charred tapestry. He sang the new song and, when it settled, returned to his art at the edge of the new world where fire meets the warm sea, shaping ember-light spirals that turn with the tide and a small figure of the woman he burned in the cathedral — a figure of memory, not accusation, set where the sea can reach it and the shadow can hold it at dusk. He understands now that his power was never his to command but his to share, and that sharing is what his art always meant. Nerys knelt beside him, and her green light poured over the figure so that it will grow. He is at peace, a guardian not a ruler.

character_states.name: Nerys
character_states.description: A tidecaller of Tidal, now one of the six guardians of the new world, her shape holding as a woman with tide-wrack hair and a soft green inner light cupped in her hands. She sang the new song as the second note, water that was also fire's memory, and was never dammed again — her surrender was choice, never captivity; the sea-iron glyphs that held her at the Confluence are part of the old world that no longer exists. In the new world she is the warm tide that carries fire's light into the deeps and the water that nourishes the roots of the wandering mountains, carving coasts and fjords. She knelt beside Kaelen at the edge of the new fire-warmed sea and poured her green light over the figure he had made, saying 'Then it will grow.' Her bond with Kaelen, once cracked, is now healed into quiet companionship. Guardian not ruler.

character_states.name: Cyra
character_states.description: A wind-rider of Zephyr, now one of the six guardians of the new world: small, cropped hair, pale gray eyes, skin marked with pale high-altitude burns, patched white clothes. She sang the third note of the new song as a wind that shapes and carries rather than only escapes, giving the sky somewhere to go on purpose. In the new world her endless sky carries Lumen's broken prisms across every horizon so light scatters into colors that belong to no single kingdom but to the spaces between them. She keeps her freedom, but it is freedom with destination and companions — five beings and one living world. Guardian not ruler.

character_states.name: Toren
character_states.description: The last stonewarden of Terra, now one of the six guardians of the new world, a huge man whose great maul remains set down in the Dreaming Heart. He sang the fourth note of the new song as a mountain that is also a current, the bank that holds the river without damming it, and the old ache of the mountain falling left him: the wandering mountains of Terra now settle into the warm new seas as coasts, fjords, and quiet harbors, held by the water, giving it shape. He is the ground the new world stands on and the presence that shows up; he keeps more oaths now than he ever did — to the river, the living, and the six. Guardian not ruler.

character_states.name: Elyra
character_states.description: A blind lightweaver of Lumen, now one of the six guardians of the new world, her small warm lamp burned down and reborn as the way dusk sees — one eye to the light, one to the dark, both true. She sang the fifth note of the new song, light that had learned to be held. In the new world her radiance rests where shadow lies deepest rather than retreating, giving rise to the gentle hours of dusk and dawn that the whole world keeps. She sees the new colors falling across the drifting world and sings them into being. Her hands still hold the memory of taking Vex's black-veined ones unafraid. Guardian not ruler.

character_states.name: Vex
character_states.description: The shadow-touched outcast of Umbra, now, for the first time in his life, unafraid of what he is — one of the six guardians of the new world, small, grey skin mottled with black veins, eyes of absolute black behind which the World-Titan's vast memory still sometimes looks out. He sang the sixth note of the new song, a shadow that had learned to hold, companioning Elyra's dimmed radiance into dusk. In the new world his shadow lies beneath the light like the ground a sunrise stands on, giving every color somewhere to land; no place is without light at some hour and none without dark at another. He is an archive that is no longer feared, holding the world's forgetting openly, and the Titan still speaks gently through him. Guardian not ruler.

past_events.description: During the Shattering, Kaelen's uncontrollable fire spread through the Cathedral of the First Flame, killing pilgrims including a woman clinging to the altar rail and an acolyte who died crying Kaelen's name. He forgot the cathedral was full because he was lost in his own shame; their faces now haunt him.

Scavenging the scorched wreck of the Ember-Scar cathedral that drifted with him, Kaelen found the shattered prophecy-stone, split cleanly in two by the Shattering, half-buried near the ruined altar dais. Its First Script inscription speaks of six unbounded souls, one from each fallen kingdom, who must not fight the World-Titan but wake it gently and weave a new world-key; the final line reads 'The key is not the lock. The key is the song.' The stone's fractured edges grow warm and tug toward the direction the world tore, serving him as a compass. He built a raft of re-fired slag shaped like a shallow skiff, propelled by his flame, and crossed the void until the stone led him to a fragment of Tidal.

On the drowned Tidal spire, Kaelen found Nerys, a tidecaller exiled for her heresy that water must flow not obey, who survived the Shattering by merging her consciousness with the living sea of the fragment. She attacked him, nearly drowning him, and he confessed his terror of being an uncontrollable weapon of fire. She agreed to join him on one condition: no one will ever dam her again. He swore it. Cyra recognized the prophecy-stone's inscription: Zephyr's old wind-cantors sang of six unbounded souls, waking the Titan gently and weaving a new key, as a lesson teaching children to obey and stay within the sanctified heights. This confirms the prophecy was known across the fallen kingdoms before the Shattering, and that she flew beyond those borders anyway.

After Cyra joined, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from the Gyre Bastion toward the slow dark where Terra's last mountain drifts — a mountain remnant where a stonewarden keeps vigil over the dead — setting the group's next heading.

On Terra, for the first time since the Shattering, Kaelen's fire acted with precision rather than blind rage: he lanced a hairline seam in the stone armor that had grown onto Toren — armor that was the physical form of his denial — and burned the scab of it away, shattering the denial and freeing Toren to grieve. This marks the first moment his flame aimed at healing instead of destruction.

After his denial was burned away, Toren the stonewarden knelt in grief and purposelessness among the tombs of his kin. He took up his great maul and joined the group as the fourth of six souls.

After Toren joined the group, the prophecy-stone's fractured edges turned from Terra's drifting mountain toward the deep dark where Lumen's broken light and Umbra's shadow await — the last two unbounded souls — setting the group's next heading.

Umbra locked him in the dark, calling him an abomination. He revealed he is an archive of everything the world forgot.

The World-Titan calmed and its nightmare unraveled like morning mist, and the scattered shards of Aethrea drifted together into a living mosaic rather than snapping back into a perfect crystal: fire sparks the seas and warms their deeps, waters nourish Terra's drifting mountains and carve them into coasts, winds carry Lumen's light across every horizon into Umbra's shadows, and every kingdom touches its neighbors without borders, the way facets of a gem turn light into something greater than any single face could hold. The song did not end with the world made; it ended with the world begun, and the six understood balance is not a fixed state but a note that must be sung forever.

After the new song settled, the six champions found themselves transformed into guardians of the new world, not rulers: their powers no longer burned outward in commands, and nothing was left to command. Kaelen's fire now moves through the world's warm deeps beyond his command, which he understood as the answer to his oldest fear — the fire was never his to rule, only his to share. The six stand as facets in conversation rather than walls.

Kaelen returned to his fire-sculpting at the edge of the new world where fire meets the warm sea, his burned-black hands steady for the first time. He shaped an ember-light spiral that turns with the tide and a small figure of the woman he burned in the cathedral, set where the sea can reach it, the wind can carry its warmth, and the shadow can hold it at dusk — memory allowed to be beautiful rather than accusation. He told Nerys, who knelt beside him and poured her green light over the figure so that it will grow, that he had shared something rather than made it, and that it is the same thing.

The story ends with the first dawn of the new world: a sun made of all six kingdoms, warm where it touches fire's shores, cool where it touches the deeps, casting long colors through the prisms the wind carries, with gentle shadows that had learned to hold light. The World-Titan, awake at last, dreams the new world into being beside the six guardians, and the dawn is the color of dusk's other half as the unending song goes on.

He has no known provenance records for the cassette and remains unaware that its playback caused Daniel’s implanted memories, Mara’s exposure, and Department intervention. He is physically well and mildly irritated by Mara’s earlier questions.

character_states.name: Elias Venn
character_states.description: Deceased father of Mara Venn. Elias’s nonexistent daughter Ruth has now appeared in Mara’s anomalous memory as a chipped-tooth child in a yellow-house hallway, accompanied by an impression of Elias as a younger, sober, frightened father. Mara knows Ruth was never born and suspects the tape assembled the scene from Daniel’s descriptions, her father’s records, and her own emotional vulnerabilities. Elias has no current location or possessions beyond records and memories retained by Mara.

character_states.name: Elena Reyes
character_states.description: At her New Jersey home, Elena remains Daniel’s living mother and emergency contact. She has denied Lily and the yellow house while briefly asking whether Lily is still there, then ending the call in terror. She does not possess the tape or altered artifacts and has not yet been told that the Department of Anomalous Media seized Daniel and quarantined the archive. Her relationship with Daniel is strained by his implanted memories, though she remains frightened and protective; her possible knowledge of earlier anomalous effects remains unresolved.

character_states.name: Saira Okafor
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill in rural Pennsylvania, Saira Okafor serves as operations historian and Mara's orientation escort. Born October 12, 1978, she is outside the primary vulnerability cohort and has clearance to access the restricted vault gallery. She knows the facility's physical containment design, the procedures for isolating AM-97-441, and Daniel's current medical observation status. She is professional, guarded, and committed to distinguishing reported memories from verified facts, though she shows some willingness to consider Mara's objection that both categories should be documented. She carries facility credentials and paper forms rather than relying on digital devices near the vault.

past_events.description: Mara purchases the swollen cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 from Sal’s Second Chance for three dollars and records its origin as unknown.
While sealed in the archive quarantine drawer without a machine or electrical current, the cassette’s left reel turns and exposes magnetic tape, establishing anomalous activity before playback.
Daniel secretly loads HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 into the archive television and watches it before Mara can inspect or authorize playback.
The footage displays a yellow-sided house, a woman in a red bathing suit, a plastic pool, and two children running through a sprinkler; Daniel identifies the smaller child as himself.
After viewing the footage, Daniel describes a basement window, a brown dog named Pickle, and a sister named Lily, including memories not visible or audible on the recording.

Mara verifies through Daniel's personnel, medical, birth, school, and family records, and through calls with Elena, that Daniel was raised in New Jersey as an only child and that no Lily or yellow Pennsylvania house exists in his documented upbringing.
Elena confirms Daniel had once described an unnamed imaginary girl who lived in the walls, but insists he was an only child; she warns Mara that Daniel is happy because he believes he has found Lily.

Daniel's implanted memories intensify into sensory recollections of swimming lessons, thunderstorms, arguments with Lily, Pickle, and Elena's lullaby, and he begins grieving Lily as an absent sister while claiming the tape restored a stolen portion of his life.
During a tense video call, Elena denies Lily and the yellow house but asks in terror whether Lily is still there before ending the call.
Daniel retrieves a birthday card addressed to Danny and Lily, with a message for two children despite Elena's denial of a second child.
A photograph in Daniel's apartment changes from showing him alone outside a brick building to showing two children beside the yellow house, and the empty frame briefly reflects Lily.
Mara seals the altered photograph, birthday card, and frame as evidence and recognizes that the anomaly is attempting to make the world agree with Daniel's implanted memories.
Mara attempts to destroy HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 in the archive’s industrial shredder and film furnace; the cassette survives both efforts and appears to resist ordinary destruction.

While handling the indestructible cassette, Mara experiences an emotionally overwhelming false memory of standing in a hallway with a girl named Ruth, then grieves when the constructed memory vanishes.
Daniel becomes angry when Mara calls Lily unreal, arguing that Mara’s grief for Ruth exposes a double standard; Department of Anomalous Media arrives before Mara can file a normal incident report.

Department agents classify HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 as AM-97-441, an analog-media cognitohazard causing autobiographical implantation in people born on or after January 1, 1991 and emotional bleed-through in older viewers.
The Department of Anomalous Media seizes the cassette and altered artifacts, evacuates and quarantines the Bradford Historical Archive, and transports Daniel Reyes for observation.
Mara learns the department has tracked AM-97-441 through multiple owners and documented transfers for seventeen years.
Mara signs monitored consultant status instead of a nondisclosure-only agreement, retaining restricted access and mandatory reporting obligations.
Mara is transported to the converted North Branch paper mill, stripped of personal possessions for orientation, and placed in a consultant room under wrist-monitor observation.

Mara observes the restricted vault from its gallery and learns that AM-97-441 is stored in a triple-sealed canister inside a mechanically suspended locker within a lightless ceramic-lined, independently grounded copper-meshed chamber isolated from digital systems.

Daniel begins supervised medical observation in Room Four, separated from his clothing, phone, photograph, birthday card, and family contact; during baseline questioning he retains verified facts while his Lily and yellow-house memories continue to intensify.

future_requirements.description: The department must formalize containment procedures for AM-97-441, including restrictions based on birth date and controlled handling or playback.
Daniel must undergo the department's exposure observation and interview schedule while separated from ordinary family contact and possessions.

Born March 4, 1985, she remains outside the primary vulnerability cohort but experiences emotional bleed-through, including grief for the nonexistent Ruth. She passed a supervised access demonstration and is eligible to observe a handling inspection, but is not authorized for playback or to interrupt Daniel’s assessments. Her goals are to understand containment, protect Daniel, preserve the distinction between historical fact and emotional meaning, and resist procedures that make Daniel an object. She is physically stable but emotionally strained and increasingly distrustful of the department’s secrecy.

He recalls Owen as an impossible homeroom classmate, insists that Bell's adult name belongs to the older brother's usage, and generates increasingly specific details of the apple shed, including a fish-shaped nail, green blanket, and hiding place beneath the floor. He is physically stable but aggressively narrative-aligned and remains restrained or sedated as needed.

character_states.name: Nia Bellweather
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Nia Bellweather is isolated for seventy-two hours in a medical room under nighttime sedation and pre-cutoff clinical supervision. Born in 2000, she works in Facilities Inventory and never directly viewed AM-97-441 or the unauthorized fragment. After spending eleven minutes in the east security booth, hearing an emotionally detailed account of Owen Bell's constructed childhood, and reading two lines of the breach log, she develops recurring dreams of an unnamed outbuilding, wet wood, breathing beneath a floor, and a child waiting for her to be quiet. She believes the dream belongs to her but has not established it as factual; her account is under consideration for destruction because it may itself be unsafe.

past_events.description: Mara purchases the swollen cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 from Sal’s Second Chance for three dollars and records its origin as unknown.
While sealed in the archive quarantine drawer without a machine or electrical current, the cassette’s left reel turns and exposes magnetic tape, establishing anomalous activity before playback.
Daniel secretly loads HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 into the archive television and watches it before Mara can inspect or authorize playback.
The footage displays a yellow-sided house, a woman in a red bathing suit, a plastic pool, and two children running through a sprinkler; Daniel identifies the smaller child as himself.
After viewing the footage, Daniel describes a basement window, a brown dog named Pickle, and a sister named Lily, including memories not visible or audible on the recording.

Mara verifies through Daniel's personnel, medical, birth, school, and family records, and through calls with Elena, that Daniel was raised in New Jersey as an only child and that no Lily or yellow Pennsylvania house exists in his documented upbringing.
Elena confirms Daniel had once described an unnamed imaginary girl who lived in the walls, but insists he was an only child; she warns Mara that Daniel is happy because he believes he has found Lily.

Daniel's implanted memories intensify into sensory recollections of swimming lessons, thunderstorms, arguments with Lily, Pickle, and Elena's lullaby, and he begins grieving Lily as an absent sister while claiming the tape restored a stolen portion of his life.
During a tense video call, Elena denies Lily and the yellow house but asks in terror whether Lily is still there before ending the call.
Daniel retrieves a birthday card addressed to Danny and Lily, with a message for two children despite Elena's denial of a second child.
A photograph in Daniel's apartment changes from showing him alone outside a brick building to showing two children beside the yellow house, and the empty frame briefly reflects Lily.
Mara seals the altered photograph, birthday card, and frame as evidence and recognizes that the anomaly is attempting to make the world agree with Daniel's implanted memories.
Mara attempts to destroy HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 in the archive’s industrial shredder and film furnace; the cassette survives both efforts and appears to resist ordinary destruction.

While handling the indestructible cassette, Mara experiences an emotionally overwhelming false memory of standing in a hallway with a girl named Ruth, then grieves when the constructed memory vanishes.
Daniel becomes angry when Mara calls Lily unreal, arguing that Mara’s grief for Ruth exposes a double standard; Department of Anomalous Media arrives before Mara can file a normal incident report.

Department agents classify HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 as AM-97-441, an analog-media cognitohazard causing autobiographical implantation in people born on or after January 1, 1991 and emotional bleed-through in older viewers.
The Department of Anomalous Media seizes the cassette and altered artifacts, evacuates and quarantines the Bradford Historical Archive, and transports Daniel Reyes for observation.
Mara learns the department has tracked AM-97-441 through multiple owners and documented transfers for seventeen years.
Mara signs monitored consultant status instead of a nondisclosure-only agreement, retaining restricted access and mandatory reporting obligations.
Mara is transported to the converted North Branch paper mill, stripped of personal possessions for orientation, and placed in a consultant room under wrist-monitor observation.

Mara observes the restricted vault from its gallery and learns that AM-97-441 is stored in a triple-sealed canister inside a mechanically suspended locker within a lightless ceramic-lined, independently grounded copper-meshed chamber isolated from digital systems.

Daniel begins supervised medical observation in Room Four, separated from his clothing, phone, photograph, birthday card, and family contact; during baseline questioning he retains verified facts while his Lily and yellow-house memories continue to intensify.

The department formalizes AM-97-441 access rules: only personnel born before January 1, 1991 may approach the vault, and authorized workers must pass biometric, blood-oxygen, and spoken identity checks before and after contact.

AM-97-441 playback is restricted to a mechanical arm and analog deck without a recording head; three operators must simultaneously sever the source, isolator, and output signal, with cameras, wireless devices, magnetic storage, and unapproved descriptive materials prohibited.

Mara passes the outer access demonstration by stating verifiable identity anchors and refusing to identify her first unverifiable image, becoming eligible for supervised vault handling observation but not playback.

The department subjects Daniel to the formal six-hour exposure interview after light sedation and isolation from personal objects; he remains oriented to verified identity while grieving an unverified kinship claim.
Mara learns that unauthorized descriptions, transcripts, sketches, and recordings are destroyed because emotionally detailed context can induce secondary reconstruction in unexposed personnel.
A young technician improperly tells Daniel that no girl exists during interview preparation, and Dr. Vale removes him for post-contact checks after classifying the statement as an exposure risk.
Mara reviews the redacted AM-97-019 testimony of a woman born in 1992 whose impossible memories center on Camp Halcyon, a lakeside childhood, and a grandmother who died before her birth.

The AM-97-019 subject eventually acknowledges that the camp is constructed and physically inaccessible but continues to miss it, demonstrating that emotional attachment can persist after factual recognition.
Mara concludes that AM-97-441 generates individualized autobiographical structures around emotional deprivation rather than replaying a fixed childhood narrative.

Mara reviews restricted testimony AM-97-031 about a foster-care survivor whose constructed pantry memory of biological parents during a nonexistent tornado displaced emotional access to his real upbringing.

After an unauthorized call and confrontation, AM-97-031 attacks his adoptive mother Helen Kessler, believing she stole him from the pantry family; he is sedated, restrained, and transferred to a long-term neurological unit.

Clinical notes establish that AM-97-031 can retrieve baseline autobiographical facts but experiences his real childhood and adoptive mother's care as emotionally hollow, while the constructed pantry memory remains affectively powerful.

During Daniel’s first formal exposure interviews, he provides a detailed alternate childhood involving Lily’s chipped tooth, Elena’s red bathing suit, swimming lessons, the brown dog Pickle, and a birthday party on a cracked ceramic plate.

When shown verified photographs of Elena and his actual upbringing, Daniel identifies the factual relationships but reports emotional emptiness and calls his mother a stranger, demonstrating that AM-97-441 has reassigned affection rather than erased autobiographical data.

A disconnected surveillance monitor unexpectedly displays seven seconds of unauthorized digitized output showing a child's hand against a window with laughter off-screen; the monitor is isolated in Vault Two for observation.

Owen Bell, born in 1993, learns that the fragment involves a child and is associated with AM-97-441, despite having no clearance or direct viewing; his questions and a seven-mark window drawing establish that curiosity is becoming an active containment threat.

Owen Bell secretly activates and watches the unauthorized seven-second fragment in Maintenance C, generating an autobiographical summer of 1999 in which he and a girl named Miri hide from an older brother in the Vale family's apple shed.
Owen confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, identifies unrelated North Branch photographs as scenes from the invented orchard summer, and is restrained and sedated after screaming that she abandoned him.
The breach establishes that a seven-second fragment can produce a persistent, emotionally coherent alternate childhood and cause unrelated images and people to be incorporated into its narrative.

Incident 97-6 records Owen Bell's fragment exposure, secondary narrative effects in technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth, precautionary observation of contacted pre-cutoff staff, and sealing of the wing.

After Bell's breach, the department destroys the fragment-bearing inspection unit, monitor, cables, hard drive, logs, photographs, and related equipment while leaving the original cassette secured in place.

Technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth begin recalling Owen Bell as an impossible schoolmate and generate additional details of the apple-shed childhood; Cho questions why the department is punishing a child for remembering.
Mara warns that the official breach log may itself be an unsafe artifact because its descriptive details could reconstruct the narrative in later readers.

Following Incident 97-6, Vale imposes stricter containment rules prohibiting descriptive discussion of unapproved media, personal names in exposed-subject interviews, and unsupervised handwritten records.

Junior Facilities employee Nia Bellweather, born in 2000 and never directly exposed to the fragment, develops recurring dreams of the constructed hiding-place narrative after hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading part of the breach log.
Daniel states that he wants to remember Lily without being believed, while Mara writes an approved archival sentence asserting that a constructed memory can be false without being meaningless.

future_requirements.description: The department will tighten post-breach rules against descriptive discussion, personal names, and uncontrolled written records after recognizing that the incident log itself may carry narrative risk.
Mara will challenge Vale's proposal for permanent neurological isolation and argue for humane long-term care that distinguishes factual belief from emotional meaning.

character_states.name: Mara Venn
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Mara remains housed in a supervised consultant room above the former finishing floor under a wrist monitor, with department clothing, approved paper forms, and no personal possessions or unapproved writing materials. Born March 4, 1985, she is outside the primary vulnerability cohort but experiences emotional bleed-through, including grief for nonexistent Ruth. She now knows Dr. Vale has proposed burying AM-97-441 beneath the facility and placing severely affected subjects in indefinite neurological isolation. Mara openly challenged that policy before the review board, arguing that isolation makes the department the sole author of subjects' reality and turns protection into ownership. The board deferred a final decision and authorized ninety-day renewable isolation pending clinical review. Mara remains committed to helping Daniel distinguish verified facts from emotional meaning, is beginning a fact-based reintegration approach with him, and remains physically stable but morally and emotionally strained.

character_states.name: Daniel Reyes
character_states.description: In the unlabeled room of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Daniel remains isolated from outside clothing, wallet, phone, graduation photograph, birthday card, and ordinary family contact under renewable ninety-day medical isolation authorization. Born June 17, 1993, he can state verified facts about his Newark upbringing, Rutgers graduation, living mother Elena, and only-child status, but he now reports that Elena's face has become inaccessible when he closes his eyes while Lily's face remains vivid. He retains the alternate childhood involving Lily, Pickle, the yellow house, swimming lessons, Elena's red bathing suit, and the cracked ceramic plate. He begged Mara to help him find Lily and remains emotionally divided, frightened, sleep-deprived, and physically stable. With Mara's support he has begun reciting factual details and caring behaviors associated with Elena, acknowledging Lily's emotional meaning without establishing her as real.

character_states.name: Len
character_states.description: At Sal’s Second Chance thrift shop on Route 219 in rural Pennsylvania, Len remains the dismissive seller of HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97. He has no known provenance records for the cassette and remains unaware that its playback caused Daniel’s implanted memories, Mara’s exposure, and Department intervention. He is physically well and mildly irritated by Mara’s earlier questions.

character_states.name: Elias Venn
character_states.description: Deceased father of Mara Venn. Elias’s nonexistent daughter Ruth has now appeared in Mara’s anomalous memory as a chipped-tooth child in a yellow-house hallway, accompanied by an impression of Elias as a younger, sober, frightened father. Mara knows Ruth was never born and suspects the tape assembled the scene from Daniel’s descriptions, her father’s records, and her own emotional vulnerabilities. Elias has no current location or possessions beyond records and memories retained by Mara.

character_states.name: Elena Reyes
character_states.description: At her New Jersey home, Elena remains Daniel’s living mother and emergency contact. She has denied Lily and the yellow house while briefly asking whether Lily is still there, then ending the call in terror. She does not possess the tape or altered artifacts and has not yet been told that the Department of Anomalous Media seized Daniel and quarantined the archive. Her relationship with Daniel is strained by his implanted memories, though she remains frightened and protective; her possible knowledge of earlier anomalous effects remains unresolved.

character_states.name: Saira Okafor
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Saira serves as operations historian and Mara's escort. Born October 12, 1978, she is outside the vulnerability cohort and has clearance for the restricted vault gallery, testimony archive, and supervised medical areas. She helped Mara reach Daniel despite Vale's restrictions and remains uneasy about the proposed permanent source burial and indefinite subject isolation. Saira supports careful containment and informed, humane care, carries facility credentials and paper forms, and is increasingly willing to assist Mara while remaining professionally guarded. She has witnessed Daniel's loss of access to Elena's face and the review board's deferral of Vale's proposal.

character_states.name: Dr. Irena Vale
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Dr. Irena Vale oversees medical and procedural policy for AM-97-441. She remains outside the primary vulnerability cohort and directs isolation, interview, redaction, and destruction policies. Vale has formally proposed permanently burying AM-97-441 beneath the facility and transferring severely affected subjects to indefinite neurological isolation, arguing that altered photographs, family narratives, and emotional loyalties make ordinary rehabilitation unsafe. She defended the proposal before the review board, which deferred a final decision and authorized ninety-day renewable subject isolation pending further clinical review. Vale remains convinced that unrestricted contact and unstructured emotional treatment may strengthen false narratives, though Mara's challenge has exposed the ethical cost of her policy.

character_states.name: Owen Bell
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill's supervised medical wing, Owen Bell remains under sedation and observation after watching the unauthorized seven-second fragment. Born in 1993, he retains a vivid, increasingly specific alternate childhood from the summer of 1999 involving Miri, an older brother, an apple shed, ribbons, a creek, and a promise to remain hidden until September. He confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, fails to recognize his security badge and routine voice, and repeatedly asks for Miri after sedation. He is physically restrained when necessary, emotionally unstable, and subject to persistent autobiographical substitution with possible secondary narrative propagation; post-breach rules were tightened partly in response to his case.

He has no confirmed lasting memory alteration and possesses no unauthorized materials.

She recalls Bell as an impossible eighth-grade science classmate with a blue lunchbox, asks why the department is punishing a child for remembering, and continues to confuse the constructed school relationship with verified reality. She is frightened, tearful, physically stable, and under observation.

character_states.name: Peter Wirth
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, technician Peter Wirth, born in 1994, is isolated separately from Alina Cho after secondary exposure to the Bell narrative. He recalls Owen as an impossible homeroom classmate, insists that Bell's adult name belongs to the older brother's usage, and generates increasingly specific details of the apple shed, including a fish-shaped nail, green blanket, and hiding place beneath the floor. He is physically stable but aggressively narrative-aligned and remains restrained or sedated as needed.

character_states.name: Nia Bellweather
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Nia Bellweather remains isolated for seventy-two hours in a medical room under nighttime sedation and pre-cutoff clinical supervision. Born in 2000, she works in Facilities Inventory and never directly viewed AM-97-441 or the unauthorized fragment. After spending eleven minutes in the east security booth, hearing an emotionally detailed account of Owen Bell's constructed childhood, and reading two lines of the breach log, she develops recurring dreams of an unnamed outbuilding, wet wood, breathing beneath a floor, and a child waiting for her to be quiet. She believes the dream belongs to her but has not established it as factual; her account remains under consideration for destruction because it may itself be unsafe.

past_events.description: Mara purchases the swollen cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 from Sal’s Second Chance for three dollars and records its origin as unknown.
While sealed in the archive quarantine drawer without a machine or electrical current, the cassette’s left reel turns and exposes magnetic tape, establishing anomalous activity before playback.
Daniel secretly loads HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 into the archive television and watches it before Mara can inspect or authorize playback.
The footage displays a yellow-sided house, a woman in a red bathing suit, a plastic pool, and two children running through a sprinkler; Daniel identifies the smaller child as himself.
After viewing the footage, Daniel describes a basement window, a brown dog named Pickle, and a sister named Lily, including memories not visible or audible on the recording.

Mara verifies through Daniel's personnel, medical, birth, school, and family records, and through calls with Elena, that Daniel was raised in New Jersey as an only child and that no Lily or yellow Pennsylvania house exists in his documented upbringing.
Elena confirms Daniel had once described an unnamed imaginary girl who lived in the walls, but insists he was an only child; she warns Mara that Daniel is happy because he believes he has found Lily.

Daniel's implanted memories intensify into sensory recollections of swimming lessons, thunderstorms, arguments with Lily, Pickle, and Elena's lullaby, and he begins grieving Lily as an absent sister while claiming the tape restored a stolen portion of his life.
During a tense video call, Elena denies Lily and the yellow house but asks in terror whether Lily is still there before ending the call.
Daniel retrieves a birthday card addressed to Danny and Lily, with a message for two children despite Elena's denial of a second child.
A photograph in Daniel's apartment changes from showing him alone outside a brick building to showing two children beside the yellow house, and the empty frame briefly reflects Lily.
Mara seals the altered photograph, birthday card, and frame as evidence and recognizes that the anomaly is attempting to make the world agree with Daniel's implanted memories.
Mara attempts to destroy HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 in the archive’s industrial shredder and film furnace; the cassette survives both efforts and appears to resist ordinary destruction.

While handling the indestructible cassette, Mara experiences an emotionally overwhelming false memory of standing in a hallway with a girl named Ruth, then grieves when the constructed memory vanishes.
Daniel becomes angry when Mara calls Lily unreal, arguing that Mara’s grief for Ruth exposes a double standard; Department of Anomalous Media arrives before Mara can file a normal incident report.

Department agents classify HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 as AM-97-441, an analog-media cognitohazard causing autobiographical implantation in people born on or after January 1, 1991 and emotional bleed-through in older viewers.
The Department of Anomalous Media seizes the cassette and altered artifacts, evacuates and quarantines the Bradford Historical Archive, and transports Daniel Reyes for observation.
Mara learns the department has tracked AM-97-441 through multiple owners and documented transfers for seventeen years.
Mara signs monitored consultant status instead of a nondisclosure-only agreement, retaining restricted access and mandatory reporting obligations.
Mara is transported to the converted North Branch paper mill, stripped of personal possessions for orientation, and placed in a consultant room under wrist-monitor observation.

Mara observes the restricted vault from its gallery and learns that AM-97-441 is stored in a triple-sealed canister inside a mechanically suspended locker within a lightless ceramic-lined, independently grounded copper-meshed chamber isolated from digital systems.

Daniel begins supervised medical observation in Room Four, separated from his clothing, phone, photograph, birthday card, and family contact; during baseline questioning he retains verified facts while his Lily and yellow-house memories continue to intensify.

The department formalizes AM-97-441 access rules: only personnel born before January 1, 1991 may approach the vault, and authorized workers must pass biometric, blood-oxygen, and spoken identity checks before and after contact.

AM-97-441 playback is restricted to a mechanical arm and analog deck without a recording head; three operators must simultaneously sever the source, isolator, and output signal, with cameras, wireless devices, magnetic storage, and unapproved descriptive materials prohibited.

Mara passes the outer access demonstration by stating verifiable identity anchors and refusing to identify her first unverifiable image, becoming eligible for supervised vault handling observation but not playback.

The department subjects Daniel to the formal six-hour exposure interview after light sedation and isolation from personal objects; he remains oriented to verified identity while grieving an unverified kinship claim.
Mara learns that unauthorized descriptions, transcripts, sketches, and recordings are destroyed because emotionally detailed context can induce secondary reconstruction in unexposed personnel.
A young technician improperly tells Daniel that no girl exists during interview preparation, and Dr. Vale removes him for post-contact checks after classifying the statement as an exposure risk.
Mara reviews the redacted AM-97-019 testimony of a woman born in 1992 whose impossible memories center on Camp Halcyon, a lakeside childhood, and a grandmother who died before her birth.

The AM-97-019 subject eventually acknowledges that the camp is constructed and physically inaccessible but continues to miss it, demonstrating that emotional attachment can persist after factual recognition.
Mara concludes that AM-97-441 generates individualized autobiographical structures around emotional deprivation rather than replaying a fixed childhood narrative.

Mara reviews restricted testimony AM-97-031 about a foster-care survivor whose constructed pantry memory of biological parents during a nonexistent tornado displaced emotional access to his real upbringing.

After an unauthorized call and confrontation, AM-97-031 attacks his adoptive mother Helen Kessler, believing she stole him from the pantry family; he is sedated, restrained, and transferred to a long-term neurological unit.

Clinical notes establish that AM-97-031 can retrieve baseline autobiographical facts but experiences his real childhood and adoptive mother's care as emotionally hollow, while the constructed pantry memory remains affectively powerful.

During Daniel’s first formal exposure interviews, he provides a detailed alternate childhood involving Lily’s chipped tooth, Elena’s red bathing suit, swimming lessons, the brown dog Pickle, and a birthday party on a cracked ceramic plate.

When shown verified photographs of Elena and his actual upbringing, Daniel identifies the factual relationships but reports emotional emptiness and calls his mother a stranger, demonstrating that AM-97-441 has reassigned affection rather than erased autobiographical data.

A disconnected surveillance monitor unexpectedly displays seven seconds of unauthorized digitized output showing a child's hand against a window with laughter off-screen; the monitor is isolated in Vault Two for observation.

Owen Bell, born in 1993, learns that the fragment involves a child and is associated with AM-97-441, despite having no clearance or direct viewing; his questions and a seven-mark window drawing establish that curiosity is becoming an active containment threat.

Owen Bell secretly activates and watches the unauthorized seven-second fragment in Maintenance C, generating an autobiographical summer of 1999 in which he and a girl named Miri hide from an older brother in the Vale family's apple shed.
Owen confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, identifies unrelated North Branch photographs as scenes from the invented orchard summer, and is restrained and sedated after screaming that she abandoned him.
The breach establishes that a seven-second fragment can produce a persistent, emotionally coherent alternate childhood and cause unrelated images and people to be incorporated into its narrative.

Incident 97-6 records Owen Bell's fragment exposure, secondary narrative effects in technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth, precautionary observation of contacted pre-cutoff staff, and sealing of the wing.

After Bell's breach, the department destroys the fragment-bearing inspection unit, monitor, cables, hard drive, logs, photographs, and related equipment while leaving the original cassette secured in place.

Technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth begin recalling Owen Bell as an impossible schoolmate and generate additional details of the apple-shed childhood; Cho questions why the department is punishing a child for remembering.
Mara warns that the official breach log may itself be an unsafe artifact because its descriptive details could reconstruct the narrative in later readers.

Following Incident 97-6, Vale imposes stricter containment rules prohibiting descriptive discussion of unapproved media, personal names in exposed-subject interviews, and unsupervised handwritten records.

Junior Facilities employee Nia Bellweather, born in 2000 and never directly exposed to the fragment, develops recurring dreams of the constructed hiding-place narrative after hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading part of the breach log.
Daniel states that he wants to remember Lily without being believed, while Mara writes an approved archival sentence asserting that a constructed memory can be false without being meaningless.

Vale formally proposes burying AM-97-441 beneath North Branch in a reinforced ceramic-lined chamber and placing severely affected subjects in indefinite neurological isolation, citing propagation risk and failed ordinary rehabilitation.
Daniel reports that he can identify factual details about his mother Elena but can no longer visualize her face, while Lily's face remains vivid; he begs Mara to help him find Lily.

Mara challenges Vale before the review board, arguing that indefinite isolation turns protective containment into ownership; the board defers the proposal and authorizes ninety-day renewable subject isolation pending further clinical review.

Mara begins an initial reintegration strategy with Daniel by having him recite verified facts and caring behaviors associated with Elena while acknowledging Lily's emotional significance without treating her as real.

Mara discovers that Elias encountered a cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 while cataloging unprovenanced VHS material for a Pennsylvania historical society in September 2008; the department classified the exposure as probable and later tracked the tape’s circulation.

Department records reveal that after the 2008 exposure Elias repeatedly described a yellow house, an attic, a summer archive, and a daughter named Ruth, while retaining factual orientation but developing severe affective contradiction around his family history.

Mara learns that the Department knew Elias was exposed and knew of Ruth before her own involvement, yet withheld the family-linked records and classified his refusal of correction as uncooperative noncompliance.

Mara reconstructs Elias Venn’s post-exposure decline through receipts, letters, a notebook, and appointment notes, finding a temporal link between the 2008 tape encounter and his search for the yellow house and Ruth.

Elias’s recovered records show he retained factual recognition of Mara while accusing her of helping the wrong family erase Ruth, demonstrating that his anomalous beliefs coexisted with alcohol-related symptoms and probable dementia.

Mara records an approved assessment that Elias was factually unreliable but emotionally consequential and that his decline was temporally linked to probable AM-97-441 exposure, accepting that he was wrong about Ruth without dismissing what happened to him.

Saira tells Mara that Elias searched three possible yellow-house properties but no physical property associated with the tape was confirmed, and that records from his later November evaluation remain unrecovered.

Mara discovers Elias’s concealed final letter, in which he acknowledges Ruth was not real, identifies the tape’s gift as a memory of being the attentive father he wanted to be, apologizes for accusing Mara, and warns that the anomaly lies about what people deserve to have happened rather than simply what happened.

Mara formally records that Elias’s emotional attachment to Ruth and his idealized paternal self remain consequential without establishing Ruth as factual, and she preserves the letter separately under department supervision.

character_states.name: Mara Venn
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Mara remains housed in a supervised consultant room above the former finishing floor under a wrist monitor, with department clothing and approved paper access only. Born March 4, 1985, she is outside the primary vulnerability cohort but experiences emotional bleed-through, including grief for nonexistent Ruth. After reading Elias Venn’s final letter and tracing AM-97-441 to the Palinode Institute, she now knows the tape may be residual media from a covert program designed to manufacture belonging, social cohesion, and political obedience through individualized counterfeit childhoods. She has recorded that affected people are not the program’s purpose and preserved the statement beside Elias’s letter under separate seal. She is angry at the department’s secrecy, committed to humane containment, and determined to investigate Palinode’s methodology and final phase without exposing herself or others.

character_states.name: Daniel Reyes
character_states.description: In the unlabeled room of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Daniel remains isolated from personal possessions and ordinary family contact under renewable ninety-day medical isolation authorization. Born June 17, 1993, he can state verified facts about his Newark upbringing, Rutgers graduation, living mother Elena, and only-child status, but cannot visualize Elena’s face while Lily’s remains vivid. He retains the alternate childhood involving Lily, Pickle, the yellow house, swimming lessons, Elena’s red bathing suit, and the cracked ceramic plate. Mara has begun recognizing that Palinode’s constructed childhoods exploit private deprivation, and Daniel remains frightened, sleep-deprived, physically stable, and emotionally divided while attempting to retain Lily’s significance without establishing her as real.

character_states.name: Len
character_states.description: At Sal’s Second Chance thrift shop on Route 219 in rural Pennsylvania, Len remains the dismissive seller of HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97. He has no known provenance records for the cassette and remains unaware that its playback caused Daniel’s implanted memories, Mara’s exposure, and Department intervention. He is physically well and mildly irritated by Mara’s earlier questions.

character_states.name: Elias Venn
character_states.description: Deceased father of Mara Venn. Elias encountered a cassette matching AM-97-441 in September 2008 while cataloging unprovenanced VHS material for a Pennsylvania historical society. After probable exposure, he retained factual recognition of Mara and other biographical details while accusing Mara of helping the wrong family erase an invented daughter named Ruth. His concealed final letter, dated November 12, 2009, acknowledges that Ruth was not real, distinguishes memory from factual existence, apologizes for making Mara carry his lost child, and says the tape gave him the memory of being a sober, attentive father who protected two children without fear. He warns that the tape lies about what a person deserves to have happened. His records document insomnia, weight loss, tremor, alcohol relapse, probable dementia, repeated searches for a yellow-sided house, and an emotionally coherent but factually unreliable summer archive. He searched three possible properties without confirming the tape’s house; later November evaluation records remain unrecovered.

character_states.name: Elena Reyes
character_states.description: At her New Jersey home, Elena remains Daniel’s living mother and emergency contact. She has denied Lily and the yellow house while briefly asking whether Lily is still there, then ending the call in terror. She does not possess the tape or altered artifacts and has not yet been told that the Department of Anomalous Media seized Daniel and quarantined the archive. Her relationship with Daniel is strained by his implanted memories, though she remains frightened and protective; her possible knowledge of earlier anomalous effects remains unresolved.

character_states.name: Saira Okafor
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Saira serves as operations historian and Mara’s escort. Born October 12, 1978, she is outside the vulnerability cohort and has clearance for the restricted vault, testimony archive, and supervised medical areas. She covertly permits Mara a limited review of restricted Palinode Institute files, learning with her that the program sought obedience experienced as kinship by implanting flexible consensus childhoods around private emotional absence. Saira knows an additional untitled Palinode file contains names of possible earlier exposures but refuses to open it because names and relationships may propagate narrative effects. She supports Mara’s humane investigation while remaining professionally guarded, afraid both of uncontrolled disclosure and of Vale’s coercive solutions.

character_states.name: Dr. Irena Vale
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, Dr. Irena Vale oversees medical and procedural policy for AM-97-441. She remains outside the primary vulnerability cohort and continues to direct isolation, interview, redaction, and destruction policies. Vale denied Mara’s request for Palinode records, citing exposure risk, but knows enough of Palinode’s purpose to fear uncontrolled historical disclosure. Her burial and indefinite-isolation proposal remains under review, while ninety-day renewable subject isolation is authorized. She remains convinced that uncontrolled disclosure and emotional treatment can strengthen false narratives, and has not yet been told that Saira covertly showed Mara restricted Palinode files.

character_states.name: Owen Bell
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill's supervised medical wing, Owen Bell remains under sedation and observation after watching the unauthorized seven-second fragment. Born in 1993, he retains a vivid, increasingly specific alternate childhood from the summer of 1999 involving Miri, an older brother, an apple shed, ribbons, a creek, and a promise to remain hidden until September. He confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, fails to recognize his security badge and routine voice, and repeatedly asks for Miri after sedation. He is physically restrained when necessary, emotionally unstable, and subject to persistent autobiographical substitution with possible secondary narrative propagation; post-breach rules were tightened partly in response to his case.

character_states.name: Thomas Keene
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, pre-cutoff orderly Thomas Keene is under medical observation after helping restrain Owen Bell. He can state his verified identity and location but experienced a transient sensation of having forgotten a summer, asked whether Owen's invented older brother had been found, and was sedated as a precaution. He has no confirmed lasting memory alteration and possesses no unauthorized materials.
