She supports humane grounding, a future supervised Elena call, and continued care rather than forced erasure, while remaining separated from AM-97-441’s relay.

character_states.name: Dr. Irena Vale
character_states.description: In the North Branch medical wing and adjoining records corridor, Vale remains active, exhausted, and factually oriented as a pre-cutoff director born in 1969. During Bell’s supervised interview she learns that Miri is not truly Vale but a protective identity Bell formed within the constructed childhood. Shaken, she revises Bell’s classification away from noncompliant hazard language and accepts continued supervision without forced erasure, while still insisting that uncontrolled exposure is dangerous. She remains responsible for containment and is beginning to recognize that affected subjects require care as persons.

character_states.name: Owen Bell
character_states.description: In Room Seven of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Owen remains sedated intermittently but awake and medically monitored, with no personal possessions except a paper cup on which he wrote Miri. Born in 1993, he can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, and increasingly distinguishes Dr. Irena Vale from Miri. He describes the apple-shed childhood and Miri as a constructed, emotionally protective part of himself—the person he became in the only childhood where he felt protected—while retaining the memory without claiming it as factual. He consents to continued supervision for now, rejects forced erasure, and remains neither cured nor wholly lost.

character_states.name: Thomas Keene
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, pre-cutoff orderly Thomas Keene remains unsteady but conscious after helping restrain Owen Bell. He can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, though he experienced a transient sensation of having forgotten a summer. During the emergency he repeated his identity anchors and helped move exposed staff away from the relay under Saira’s direction. He has no confirmed lasting memory alteration, no possessions, and remains under medical observation and grounding protocols.

character_states.name: Alina Cho
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room medical area under pre-cutoff supervision, Alina remains frightened but more verbally settled after her controlled interview, with no personal possessions. Born February 3, 1994, she can state her identity, work in facilities, scar on her left thumb, and location. She accepts that Owen Bell was not factually her schoolmate while insisting that the kindness she remembers remains something that happened in her, and asks that it be preserved without becoming a factual claim. She remains separated from the source and requires grounding and observation.

character_states.name: Peter Wirth
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room medical area under pre-cutoff supervision, Peter remains agitated and emotionally defensive, with a bandaged hand and no personal possessions. Born November 9, 1994, he can state that his sister Rebecca lives in Ohio and that the concrete-room childhood is not factually verifiable, though he still cannot reliably picture Rebecca's face. He rejects the department's symbolic-integration language, demands acknowledgment that the constructed memory is part of his identity without calling it factual, and refuses consent for another interview. He remains separated from the relay and requires humane grounding and clinical care.

character_states.name: Nia Bellweather
character_states.description: Nia remains isolated for seventy-two hours in a medical room at North Branch under nighttime sedation and pre-cutoff clinical supervision. Born in 2000, she never directly viewed AM-97-441 or the unauthorized fragment and has not viewed the Palinode final recording. After hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading two lines of the breach log, she continues recurring dreams of an unnamed outbuilding, wet wood, breathing beneath a floor, and a waiting child. She believes the dream belongs to her but has not established it as factual; her account remains potentially unsafe and she possesses no personal materials.

past_events.description: Mara purchases the swollen cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 from Sal’s Second Chance for three dollars and records its origin as unknown.
While sealed in the archive quarantine drawer without a machine or electrical current, the cassette’s left reel turns and exposes magnetic tape, establishing anomalous activity before playback.
Daniel secretly loads HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 into the archive television and watches it before Mara can inspect or authorize playback.
The footage displays a yellow-sided house, a woman in a red bathing suit, a plastic pool, and two children running through a sprinkler; Daniel identifies the smaller child as himself.
After viewing the footage, Daniel describes a basement window, a brown dog named Pickle, and a sister named Lily, including memories not visible or audible on the recording.

Mara verifies through Daniel's personnel, medical, birth, school, and family records, and through calls with Elena, that Daniel was raised in New Jersey as an only child and that no Lily or yellow Pennsylvania house exists in his documented upbringing.
Elena confirms Daniel had once described an unnamed imaginary girl who lived in the walls, but insists he was an only child; she warns Mara that Daniel is happy because he believes he has found Lily.

Daniel's implanted memories intensify into sensory recollections of swimming lessons, thunderstorms, arguments with Lily, Pickle, and Elena's lullaby, and he begins grieving Lily as an absent sister while claiming the tape restored a stolen portion of his life.
During a tense video call, Elena denies Lily and the yellow house but asks in terror whether Lily is still there before ending the call.
Daniel retrieves a birthday card addressed to Danny and Lily, with a message for two children despite Elena's denial of a second child.
A photograph in Daniel's apartment changes from showing him alone outside a brick building to showing two children beside the yellow house, and the empty frame briefly reflects Lily.
Mara seals the altered photograph, birthday card, and frame as evidence and recognizes that the anomaly is attempting to make the world agree with Daniel's implanted memories.
Mara attempts to destroy HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 in the archive’s industrial shredder and film furnace; the cassette survives both efforts and appears to resist ordinary destruction.

While handling the indestructible cassette, Mara experiences an emotionally overwhelming false memory of standing in a hallway with a girl named Ruth, then grieves when the constructed memory vanishes.
Daniel becomes angry when Mara calls Lily unreal, arguing that Mara’s grief for Ruth exposes a double standard; Department of Anomalous Media arrives before Mara can file a normal incident report.

Department agents classify HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 as AM-97-441, an analog-media cognitohazard causing autobiographical implantation in people born on or after January 1, 1991 and emotional bleed-through in older viewers.
The Department of Anomalous Media seizes the cassette and altered artifacts, evacuates and quarantines the Bradford Historical Archive, and transports Daniel Reyes for observation.
Mara learns the department has tracked AM-97-441 through multiple owners and documented transfers for seventeen years.
Mara signs monitored consultant status instead of a nondisclosure-only agreement, retaining restricted access and mandatory reporting obligations.
Mara is transported to the converted North Branch paper mill, stripped of personal possessions for orientation, and placed in a consultant room under wrist-monitor observation.

Mara observes the restricted vault from its gallery and learns that AM-97-441 is stored in a triple-sealed canister inside a mechanically suspended locker within a lightless ceramic-lined, independently grounded copper-meshed chamber isolated from digital systems.

Daniel begins supervised medical observation in Room Four, separated from his clothing, phone, photograph, birthday card, and family contact; during baseline questioning he retains verified facts while his Lily and yellow-house memories continue to intensify.

The department formalizes AM-97-441 access rules: only personnel born before January 1, 1991 may approach the vault, and authorized workers must pass biometric, blood-oxygen, and spoken identity checks before and after contact.

AM-97-441 playback is restricted to a mechanical arm and analog deck without a recording head; three operators must simultaneously sever the source, isolator, and output signal, with cameras, wireless devices, magnetic storage, and unapproved descriptive materials prohibited.

Mara passes the outer access demonstration by stating verifiable identity anchors and refusing to identify her first unverifiable image, becoming eligible for supervised vault handling observation but not playback.

The department subjects Daniel to the formal six-hour exposure interview after light sedation and isolation from personal objects; he remains oriented to verified identity while grieving an unverified kinship claim.
Mara learns that unauthorized descriptions, transcripts, sketches, and recordings are destroyed because emotionally detailed context can induce secondary reconstruction in unexposed personnel.
A young technician improperly tells Daniel that no girl exists during interview preparation, and Dr. Vale removes him for post-contact checks after classifying the statement as an exposure risk.
Mara reviews the redacted AM-97-019 testimony of a woman born in 1992 whose impossible memories center on Camp Halcyon, a lakeside childhood, and a grandmother who died before her birth.

The AM-97-019 subject eventually acknowledges that the camp is constructed and physically inaccessible but continues to miss it, demonstrating that emotional attachment can persist after factual recognition.
Mara concludes that AM-97-441 generates individualized autobiographical structures around emotional deprivation rather than replaying a fixed childhood narrative.

Mara reviews restricted testimony AM-97-031 about a foster-care survivor whose constructed pantry memory of biological parents during a nonexistent tornado displaced emotional access to his real upbringing.

After an unauthorized call and confrontation, AM-97-031 attacks his adoptive mother Helen Kessler, believing she stole him from the pantry family; he is sedated, restrained, and transferred to a long-term neurological unit.

Clinical notes establish that AM-97-031 can retrieve baseline autobiographical facts but experiences his real childhood and adoptive mother's care as emotionally hollow, while the constructed pantry memory remains affectively powerful.

During Daniel’s first formal exposure interviews, he provides a detailed alternate childhood involving Lily’s chipped tooth, Elena’s red bathing suit, swimming lessons, the brown dog Pickle, and a birthday party on a cracked ceramic plate.

When shown verified photographs of Elena and his actual upbringing, Daniel identifies the factual relationships but reports emotional emptiness and calls his mother a stranger, demonstrating that AM-97-441 has reassigned affection rather than erased autobiographical data.

A disconnected surveillance monitor unexpectedly displays seven seconds of unauthorized digitized output showing a child's hand against a window with laughter off-screen; the monitor is isolated in Vault Two for observation.

Owen Bell, born in 1993, learns that the fragment involves a child and is associated with AM-97-441, despite having no clearance or direct viewing; his questions and a seven-mark window drawing establish that curiosity is becoming an active containment threat.

Owen Bell secretly activates and watches the unauthorized seven-second fragment in Maintenance C, generating an autobiographical summer of 1999 in which he and a girl named Miri hide from an older brother in the Vale family's apple shed.
Owen confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, identifies unrelated North Branch photographs as scenes from the invented orchard summer, and is restrained and sedated after screaming that she abandoned him.
The breach establishes that a seven-second fragment can produce a persistent, emotionally coherent alternate childhood and cause unrelated images and people to be incorporated into its narrative.

Incident 97-6 records Owen Bell's fragment exposure, secondary narrative effects in technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth, precautionary observation of contacted pre-cutoff staff, and sealing of the wing.

After Bell's breach, the department destroys the fragment-bearing inspection unit, monitor, cables, hard drive, logs, photographs, and related equipment while leaving the original cassette secured in place.

Technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth begin recalling Owen Bell as an impossible schoolmate and generate additional details of the apple-shed childhood; Cho questions why the department is punishing a child for remembering.
Mara warns that the official breach log may itself be an unsafe artifact because its descriptive details could reconstruct the narrative in later readers.

Following Incident 97-6, Vale imposes stricter containment rules prohibiting descriptive discussion of unapproved media, personal names in exposed-subject interviews, and unsupervised handwritten records.

Junior Facilities employee Nia Bellweather, born in 2000 and never directly exposed to the fragment, develops recurring dreams of the constructed hiding-place narrative after hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading part of the breach log.
Daniel states that he wants to remember Lily without being believed, while Mara writes an approved archival sentence asserting that a constructed memory can be false without being meaningless.

Vale formally proposes burying AM-97-441 beneath North Branch in a reinforced ceramic-lined chamber and placing severely affected subjects in indefinite neurological isolation, citing propagation risk and failed ordinary rehabilitation.
Daniel reports that he can identify factual details about his mother Elena but can no longer visualize her face, while Lily's face remains vivid; he begs Mara to help him find Lily.

Mara challenges Vale before the review board, arguing that indefinite isolation turns protective containment into ownership; the board defers the proposal and authorizes ninety-day renewable subject isolation pending further clinical review.

Mara begins an initial reintegration strategy with Daniel by having him recite verified facts and caring behaviors associated with Elena while acknowledging Lily's emotional significance without treating her as real.

Mara discovers that Elias encountered a cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 while cataloging unprovenanced VHS material for a Pennsylvania historical society in September 2008; the department classified the exposure as probable and later tracked the tape’s circulation.

Department records reveal that after the 2008 exposure Elias repeatedly described a yellow house, an attic, a summer archive, and a daughter named Ruth, while retaining factual orientation but developing severe affective contradiction around his family history.

Mara learns that the Department knew Elias was exposed and knew of Ruth before her own involvement, yet withheld the family-linked records and classified his refusal of correction as uncooperative noncompliance.

Mara reconstructs Elias Venn’s post-exposure decline through receipts, letters, a notebook, and appointment notes, finding a temporal link between the 2008 tape encounter and his search for the yellow house and Ruth.

Elias’s recovered records show he retained factual recognition of Mara while accusing her of helping the wrong family erase Ruth, demonstrating that his anomalous beliefs coexisted with alcohol-related symptoms and probable dementia.

Mara records an approved assessment that Elias was factually unreliable but emotionally consequential and that his decline was temporally linked to probable AM-97-441 exposure, accepting that he was wrong about Ruth without dismissing what happened to him.

Saira tells Mara that Elias searched three possible yellow-house properties but no physical property associated with the tape was confirmed, and that records from his later November evaluation remain unrecovered.

Mara discovers Elias’s concealed final letter, in which he acknowledges Ruth was not real, identifies the tape’s gift as a memory of being the attentive father he wanted to be, apologizes for accusing Mara, and warns that the anomaly lies about what people deserve to have happened rather than simply what happened.

Mara formally records that Elias’s emotional attachment to Ruth and his idealized paternal self remain consequential without establishing Ruth as factual, and she preserves the letter separately under department supervision.

Mara and Saira locate restricted Palinode Institute files identifying AM-97-441 as residual media from a behavioral program intended to manufacture belonging and voluntary political compliance through shared but individualized childhood nostalgia.

Palinode’s final-phase documents establish that researchers used private emotional absence, consumer VHS conventions, and flexible autobiographical prompts rather than identical memories, with a yellow-sided house appearing as a recurring legitimacy symbol.

Saira tells Mara that Palinode’s objective was obedience experienced as kinship, while Mara records that affected people are not the program’s purpose and preserves the statement beside Elias’s letter under separate seal.

Mara studies a controlled Palinode methodology file documenting visual entrainment, VHS defects, guided recollection, memory drugs, social reinforcement, and flexible emotional templates that caused subjects to generate incompatible families and seek to inhabit constructed childhoods.

Mara concludes that AM-97-441 may be a calibration reel designed to make viewers supply their own emotional absences and autobiographical details, rather than a conventional home movie with fixed content.

Palinode case records reveal exposed subjects abandoning legal identities, pursuing constructed homes and families, and treating resistance to reintegration as evidence of successful attachment; one case is linked to the previously reviewed pantry testimony.
Mara begins using a non-descriptive fact-based grounding gesture with Daniel, prompting him to remain oriented to the present without denying Lily’s emotional significance.

Saira gives Mara restricted access to the 1997 anchor-date file, establishing that July 19, 1997 was selected as a functional temporal anchor for consumer VHS distribution rather than as a historically significant date.

The Palinode final phase planned to seed mass-market VHS tapes through thrift shops, estate sales, church rummage events, and liquidation auctions, disguising calibration material as discovered home movies.

During the July 19, 1997 comparison trial, technician R. Bell was exposed and identified laboratory director Adrian Kessler as her deceased son Matthew; the incident escalated into a fire that officially closed the Palinode Institute, with Kessler presumed dead and Bell later dying under prolonged sedation.

After the Palinode fire, attempted destruction of surviving cassettes and equipment produced anomalous persistence, including replay after erasure, self-rewound tape, and a seven-second audio loop from furnace ash, leading the department to suspend ordinary disposal.

The Department of Anomalous Media inherited surviving Palinode consumer cassettes, research notes, and damaged playback equipment, separating the material among secure sites and placing the presumed source in suspension.

Saira shares Daniel’s latest assessments, which recommend controlled symbolic integration: subjects may retain emotionally significant constructed figures while distinguishing literal belief from personal meaning.

During a supervised grounding session, Daniel identifies verified facts about his Newark upbringing and mother Elena, acknowledges Lily did not exist as his sister, and identifies Lily’s hand on his shoulder during an unverified thunderstorm memory as representing someone who knew he was afraid.

Dr. Irena Vale reveals that an earlier anomalous-media exposure in her family home in 1981 fractured her parents’ and brother Paul’s autobiographical identities, destroyed the family’s relationships, and left Paul unable to recognize her for decades.

Vale identifies the earlier household tape as a pre-VHS calibration medium with behavior matching AM-97-441; her father’s destruction attempt produced radio playback from the ash, linking her personal history to Palinode-type persistence.

Owen Bell accurately reproduces private details of Vale’s real apple shed and family repairs, including the swollen west door, copper-wire hinge, green blanket, late-blooming tree, and red ribbon, despite not having access to her records.

Mara argues that AM-97-441 may assemble narrative fragments from nearby people rather than merely parasitize an individual host, and Vale orders her family details source-isolated and removes the phrase apple shed from the active incident summary.

Mara and Saira secretly establish an unauthorized plan to use the tape transfer as a controlled confrontation, with informed consent, pre-cutoff interviewers, signal severance, and separate post-contact grounding rooms.
Daniel explicitly consents to confront the constructed material after being told it is unsafe and stoppable, while retaining factual anchors and requesting one fact-based interview afterward.

Owen Bell gives qualified spoken consent to confront his constructed childhood after being informed that Miri may not be real and that the signal can be stopped, though his understanding remains unstable.
Saira prepares and memorizes a transfer route from the medical wing through the vault to the burial elevator, including separate interview and emergency sedation rooms, then destroys the route map.

Vale discovers a faint unauthorized vault-access impression bearing Saira Okafor’s initials, treats it as evidence of procedural compromise, and accelerates the source transfer and burial to 14:00 the same day.
Vale removes Saira from medical-wing and vault duties, suspends her clearance, and assigns her to source-isolated administrative work pending review.
Vale orders Daniel transferred from Room Four to a more isolated neurological unit with no shared ventilation, plumbing, or staff rotation, despite acknowledging that he has committed no infraction.

Mara establishes that the Department has no discharge criteria, reintegration schedule, family counseling, legal advocacy, or long-term care plan for subjects whose factual memories remain accessible while emotional attachments have been displaced.

Vale’s burial memorandum states that once AM-97-441 is buried, active studies of symbolic integration, emotional retention, and post-exposure reintegration will be suspended, revealing burial as both containment and institutional closure of the ethical debate.

During the accelerated burial, the elevator stops between floors and the mechanical playback deck activates without authorization even after the output relay and building intercom breakers are disconnected.
AM-97-441 audio propagates through the North Branch intercom and emergency devices as static, children’s laughter, pool water, and distant voices despite the facility’s severance attempts.

Personnel born after the vulnerability cutoff begin perceiving personalized childhood locations and recasting coworkers as relatives, teachers, enemies, and lost friends, causing the lockdown and identity checks to fail across the mill.
Mara and Saira reestablish contact through their prearranged three-two-three knocking pattern, confirming that the burial order remains incomplete while the source continues activating the facility.

During the active transfer breach, vulnerable personnel perceive North Branch as individualized summer camps, homes, churches, hospitals, and other childhood settings; facility maps, doors, uniforms, and identities cease to agree across observers, disrupting coordinated security response.

Saira reaches exposed personnel in the emergency corridors and grounds them by repeating their names, birth dates, location, bodily sensations, and other verifiable present facts without arguing with their personalized perceptions.

Mara and Saira, with Vale’s factual confirmation, descend toward the neurological unit and locate Daniel inside a composite yellow-room setting where the anomaly presents a false family and Lily’s voice urges Mara that she has arrived too late.

Inside the composite yellow room, Daniel encounters Lily as an older girl who identifies herself as the part of him that has waited for someone to admit his loneliness, rather than as a literal sister trapped in the tape.

Mara and Saira ground Daniel with verifiable facts about his Newark upbringing, Elena, Rutgers, and North Branch; Daniel acknowledges his loneliness, consents to remain in the present, and refuses to follow Lily into the constructed yellow house while retaining love for what she represents.

During the active breach, Mara experiences Ruth as a lost sister beside Elias, then recognizes the figure’s face and details as an assembled construction using her childhood photographs, Daniel’s Lily descriptions, and Palinode’s yellow-house conventions; she rejects calling Ruth factual while preserving the grief as emotionally real.

Through the unstable relay, Mara, Saira, and Daniel view Palinode’s final research recording, which identifies the program’s goal as using nostalgia to make subjects surrender the present to whoever defines the past and confirms that adaptive longing produced individualized counterfeit childhoods instead of ideological consensus.

The Palinode recording warns that conventional destruction and burial may not be neutral, distinguishes emotional persistence from factual validity, and instructs future handlers to record the subject’s want while rejecting the authority attached to it.

The unstable relay reaches the end of the recording and immediately begins again, while the disconnected vault reel continues turning and the yellow-house image remains active, confirming that the source can cycle its final sequence without a functioning conventional motor.

Mara, Saira, and Daniel prevent Vale’s blind incineration order, interrupt the suspension-locker transfer, and route AM-97-441’s active output into a localized inspection channel instead of the facility intercom.
Vale authorizes the controlled channel while retaining destruction as a witnessed contingency; pre-cutoff personnel move exposed staff away from the relay and begin grounding and subject checks.

The first controlled inspection-channel interviews are conducted under informed consent, with each subject stating present verifiable facts before being invited to distinguish an emotional truth from the constructed childhood narrative.

Daniel identifies Lily as a constructed figure and says she represents the person he invented so he would not be the only one who knew he was lonely; he stops after eleven minutes and requests that the record note he stopped rather than failed.

Alina Cho identifies the constructed school narrative as representing the wish that someone could disappear while people still remembered him, and asks that her memory of being treated kindly be preserved without asserting Owen Bell was factually her classmate.

Peter Wirth identifies the constructed hiding place as representing a place where fear meant someone would come, but rejects the interview framework and accuses the department of stealing his proof that anyone would come.

Mara's handwritten source-isolated notes establish that factual correction does not dissolve attachment, grief survives recognition, and testimony can remain precise without granting a constructed narrative authority.

In the controlled inspection interviews, the lakeside-camp subject acknowledges that her grandmother associated with Camp Halcyon never lived, while choosing to retain her as a named internal story without making a factual claim.

The former foster-care subject rejects the belief that Helen Kessler stole him, but retains the constructed pantry memory as part of his identity and as a representation of wanting protection; he asks the record to distinguish his own change from departmental correction.
Alina Cho accepts that Owen Bell was not factually her schoolmate while insisting that the kindness she remembers remains an event in her own emotional life.

Peter Wirth refuses symbolic-integration language, demands that the department acknowledge the concrete-room memory as part of his identity without calling it factual, and declines consent for another interview.
Mara and Saira amend the rights ledger to distinguish factual status from subject meaning and to preserve subjects' own language about retained constructed memories.

During a supervised interview, Owen Bell distinguishes Dr. Irena Vale from Miri, identifying Miri as the protective part of himself formed by the constructed childhood; he accepts continued supervision without forced erasure while retaining the apple-shed memory as nonliteral and emotionally meaningful.

Dr. Vale revises Bell’s clinical classification from noncompliant to subject under supervision, documenting emerging factual distinction, retained emotional attachment, and neither cure nor total loss.

During a supervised session, Daniel recounts verifiable details of his Newark apartment and Elena’s practical care, recognizes that his adolescent loneliness was real without making Lily factual, and distinguishes Elena’s imperfect efforts from the constructed family narrative.

Daniel writes on a paper cup, “Lily is not real,” followed by “I do not have to stop loving her,” and consents in principle to a future call with Elena while postponing it after staff observe excessive emotional and physical strain.

future_requirements.description: After the crisis, Mara and Saira must establish a durable care and rights framework for affected subjects whose factual memories remain accessible but whose emotional attachments have been displaced, rather than leaving them under indefinite renewable isolation.

character_states.name: Mara Venn
character_states.description: In the North Branch paper mill’s medical-wing corridor and source-isolated records area, Mara remains physically exhausted but factually oriented as a pre-cutoff consultant born March 4, 1985. She wears monitored facility clothing and has supervised paper, pencil, and gloves but no personal possessions. After opposing Vale’s burial and indefinite isolation plan, she helps establish the revised care-and-rights framework, preserves subjects’ own wording in the new rights ledger, and supports Daniel’s future supervised contact with Elena. She knows AM-97-441 has been resealed without playback in a stricter isolated vault, that no copies are being made, and that factual status must be separated from emotional meaning. She remains committed to humane containment and affected subjects’ autonomy, though strained by the continuing danger.

character_states.name: Daniel Reyes
character_states.description: In Room Four-B of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Daniel remains physically exhausted but oriented and monitored, born June 17, 1993. He has no personal possessions except the paper cup bearing his statement that Lily is not real and that he does not have to stop loving her; his wording is also preserved in the source-isolated rights ledger. He can state his Newark upbringing, living mother Elena, Rutgers education, and current location, while understanding Lily as a symbolic companion representing the family and witness he needed rather than a factual sister. He has requested assistance rebuilding contact with Elena when medically appropriate, accepts continued source-separated care, and requires compassionate grounding without forced erasure.

character_states.name: Len
character_states.description: At Sal’s Second Chance thrift shop on Route 219 in rural Pennsylvania, Len remains the dismissive seller of HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97. He has no known provenance records for the cassette and remains unaware that its playback caused Daniel’s implanted memories, Mara’s exposure, and Department intervention. He is physically well and mildly irritated by Mara’s earlier questions.

character_states.name: Elias Venn
character_states.description: Deceased father of Mara Venn. Elias encountered a cassette matching AM-97-441 in September 2008 while cataloging unprovenanced VHS material for a Pennsylvania historical society. After probable exposure, he retained factual recognition of Mara and other biographical details while accusing Mara of helping the wrong family erase an invented daughter named Ruth. His concealed final letter acknowledges Ruth was not real, distinguishes memory from factual existence, apologizes for making Mara carry his lost child, and says the tape gave him the memory of being a sober, attentive father who protected two children without fear. His warning that the tape lies about what people deserve to have happened now informs Mara’s interpretation of Bell’s case and Palinode’s method. His records document insomnia, weight loss, tremor, alcohol relapse, probable dementia, repeated searches for a yellow-sided house, and an emotionally coherent but factually unreliable summer archive. He is deceased and remains central to Mara’s understanding of emotional consequence without factual verification.

character_states.name: Elena Reyes
character_states.description: At her New Jersey home, Elena remains Daniel’s living mother and emergency contact, frightened and emotionally strained but protective. She knows Daniel is asking about Lily and has agreed in principle to a supervised call, including saying Lily’s name when asked, though the call has not yet occurred. She remains unaware of the Department’s full containment history and has not possessed the tape or altered artifacts. Her relationship with Daniel is tense because of his implanted memories, but she remains connected to his care and may hold unresolved knowledge about earlier anomalous effects.

character_states.name: Saira Okafor
character_states.description: In the North Branch medical wing, source-isolated records area, and adjoining vault control station, Saira remains fatigued but physically capable, born October 12, 1978, wearing monitored facility clothing and possessing only supervised paper, pencil, gloves, and authorized control materials. She co-leads the emergency review that suspends indefinite isolation, establishes thirty-day clinical reviews, informed consent, independent oversight, long-term psychological care, and source-separated supervised rooms. She helps reseal AM-97-441 without playback and maintains the rights ledger separating factual claims from subject-owned meaning. She monitors Daniel, Owen, Alina, Peter, and other affected personnel, supports Daniel’s future supervised call with Elena, and remains determined to make containment care rather than punishment.

character_states.name: Dr. Irena Vale
character_states.description: In the North Branch records corridor and vault-control area, Vale remains active, exhausted, and factually oriented as a pre-cutoff director born in 1969. She retains responsibility for immediate containment and helped authorize resealing AM-97-441 without playback, but her burial order and plan for indefinite neurological isolation were suspended by the emergency review. Shaken by Bell’s distinction between Miri and herself and challenged by Mara and Saira, she accepts—reluctantly—that affected subjects require supervised care, consent, review, and rights rather than permanent classification as hazards. She remains emotionally defensive and still believes uncontrolled exposure is dangerous, while facing growing conflict with the revised humane framework.

character_states.name: Owen Bell
character_states.description: In Room Seven of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Owen remains intermittently sedated but awake and medically monitored, born in 1993, with no personal possessions except the paper cup on which he wrote Miri. He can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, and distinguishes Dr. Irena Vale from Miri, the protective identity formed within the constructed childhood. His apple-shed memories remain nonliteral but emotionally meaningful. He is now classified as a subject under supervised care rather than noncompliant, remains source-separated, and consents to continued monitoring without forced erasure.

character_states.name: Thomas Keene
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, pre-cutoff orderly Thomas Keene remains unsteady but conscious after helping restrain Owen Bell. He can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, though he experienced a transient sensation of having forgotten a summer. During the emergency he repeated his identity anchors and helped move exposed staff away from the relay under Saira’s direction. He has no confirmed lasting memory alteration, no possessions, and remains under medical observation and grounding protocols.

character_states.name: Alina Cho
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room supervised medical area, Alina remains frightened but verbally settled and source-separated, born February 3, 1994, with no personal possessions. She can state her identity, work in facilities, scar on her left thumb, and location. She accepts that Owen Bell was not factually her schoolmate while insisting that the kindness she remembers remains an event in her own emotional life. She has dictated that distinction into the new rights ledger, remains under psychological and medical observation, and may refuse further interviews.

character_states.name: Peter Wirth
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room supervised medical area, Peter remains agitated and emotionally defensive, born November 9, 1994, with a bandaged hand and no personal possessions. He can state that his sister Rebecca lives in Ohio and that the concrete-room childhood is not factually verifiable, though he still cannot reliably picture Rebecca’s face. He rejects symbolic-integration language, demands acknowledgment that the constructed memory is part of his identity without calling it factual, and has refused to dictate a meaning statement beyond recording his refusal. He remains source-separated and entitled to clinical care, review, and independent advocacy.

character_states.name: Nia Bellweather
character_states.description: Nia remains isolated for seventy-two hours in a medical room at North Branch under nighttime sedation and pre-cutoff clinical supervision. Born in 2000, she never directly viewed AM-97-441 or the unauthorized fragment and has not viewed the Palinode final recording. After hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading two lines of the breach log, she continues recurring dreams of an unnamed outbuilding, wet wood, breathing beneath a floor, and a waiting child. She believes the dream belongs to her but has not established it as factual; her account remains potentially unsafe and she possesses no personal materials.

After viewing the footage, Daniel describes a basement window, a brown dog named Pickle, and a sister named Lily, including memories not visible or audible on the recording.

Mara verifies through Daniel's personnel, medical, birth, school, and family records, and through calls with Elena, that Daniel was raised in New Jersey as an only child and that no Lily or yellow Pennsylvania house exists in his documented upbringing.
Elena confirms Daniel had once described an unnamed imaginary girl who lived in the walls, but insists he was an only child; she warns Mara that Daniel is happy because he believes he has found Lily.

Daniel's implanted memories intensify into sensory recollections of swimming lessons, thunderstorms, arguments with Lily, Pickle, and Elena's lullaby, and he begins grieving Lily as an absent sister while claiming the tape restored a stolen portion of his life.
During a tense video call, Elena denies Lily and the yellow house but asks in terror whether Lily is still there before ending the call.
Daniel retrieves a birthday card addressed to Danny and Lily, with a message for two children despite Elena's denial of a second child.
A photograph in Daniel's apartment changes from showing him alone outside a brick building to showing two children beside the yellow house, and the empty frame briefly reflects Lily.
Mara seals the altered photograph, birthday card, and frame as evidence and recognizes that the anomaly is attempting to make the world agree with Daniel's implanted memories.
Mara attempts to destroy HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 in the archive’s industrial shredder and film furnace; the cassette survives both efforts and appears to resist ordinary destruction.

While handling the indestructible cassette, Mara experiences an emotionally overwhelming false memory of standing in a hallway with a girl named Ruth, then grieves when the constructed memory vanishes.
Daniel becomes angry when Mara calls Lily unreal, arguing that Mara’s grief for Ruth exposes a double standard; Department of Anomalous Media arrives before Mara can file a normal incident report.

Department agents classify HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 as AM-97-441, an analog-media cognitohazard causing autobiographical implantation in people born on or after January 1, 1991 and emotional bleed-through in older viewers.
The Department of Anomalous Media seizes the cassette and altered artifacts, evacuates and quarantines the Bradford Historical Archive, and transports Daniel Reyes for observation.
Mara learns the department has tracked AM-97-441 through multiple owners and documented transfers for seventeen years.
Mara signs monitored consultant status instead of a nondisclosure-only agreement, retaining restricted access and mandatory reporting obligations.
Mara is transported to the converted North Branch paper mill, stripped of personal possessions for orientation, and placed in a consultant room under wrist-monitor observation.

Mara observes the restricted vault from its gallery and learns that AM-97-441 is stored in a triple-sealed canister inside a mechanically suspended locker within a lightless ceramic-lined, independently grounded copper-meshed chamber isolated from digital systems.

Daniel begins supervised medical observation in Room Four, separated from his clothing, phone, photograph, birthday card, and family contact; during baseline questioning he retains verified facts while his Lily and yellow-house memories continue to intensify.

The department formalizes AM-97-441 access rules: only personnel born before January 1, 1991 may approach the vault, and authorized workers must pass biometric, blood-oxygen, and spoken identity checks before and after contact.

AM-97-441 playback is restricted to a mechanical arm and analog deck without a recording head; three operators must simultaneously sever the source, isolator, and output signal, with cameras, wireless devices, magnetic storage, and unapproved descriptive materials prohibited.

Mara passes the outer access demonstration by stating verifiable identity anchors and refusing to identify her first unverifiable image, becoming eligible for supervised vault handling observation but not playback.

The department subjects Daniel to the formal six-hour exposure interview after light sedation and isolation from personal objects; he remains oriented to verified identity while grieving an unverified kinship claim.
Mara learns that unauthorized descriptions, transcripts, sketches, and recordings are destroyed because emotionally detailed context can induce secondary reconstruction in unexposed personnel.
A young technician improperly tells Daniel that no girl exists during interview preparation, and Dr. Vale removes him for post-contact checks after classifying the statement as an exposure risk.
Mara reviews the redacted AM-97-019 testimony of a woman born in 1992 whose impossible memories center on Camp Halcyon, a lakeside childhood, and a grandmother who died before her birth.

The AM-97-019 subject eventually acknowledges that the camp is constructed and physically inaccessible but continues to miss it, demonstrating that emotional attachment can persist after factual recognition.
Mara concludes that AM-97-441 generates individualized autobiographical structures around emotional deprivation rather than replaying a fixed childhood narrative.

Mara reviews restricted testimony AM-97-031 about a foster-care survivor whose constructed pantry memory of biological parents during a nonexistent tornado displaced emotional access to his real upbringing.

After an unauthorized call and confrontation, AM-97-031 attacks his adoptive mother Helen Kessler, believing she stole him from the pantry family; he is sedated, restrained, and transferred to a long-term neurological unit.

Clinical notes establish that AM-97-031 can retrieve baseline autobiographical facts but experiences his real childhood and adoptive mother's care as emotionally hollow, while the constructed pantry memory remains affectively powerful.

During Daniel’s first formal exposure interviews, he provides a detailed alternate childhood involving Lily’s chipped tooth, Elena’s red bathing suit, swimming lessons, the brown dog Pickle, and a birthday party on a cracked ceramic plate.

When shown verified photographs of Elena and his actual upbringing, Daniel identifies the factual relationships but reports emotional emptiness and calls his mother a stranger, demonstrating that AM-97-441 has reassigned affection rather than erased autobiographical data.

A disconnected surveillance monitor unexpectedly displays seven seconds of unauthorized digitized output showing a child's hand against a window with laughter off-screen; the monitor is isolated in Vault Two for observation.

Owen Bell, born in 1993, learns that the fragment involves a child and is associated with AM-97-441, despite having no clearance or direct viewing; his questions and a seven-mark window drawing establish that curiosity is becoming an active containment threat.

Owen Bell secretly activates and watches the unauthorized seven-second fragment in Maintenance C, generating an autobiographical summer of 1999 in which he and a girl named Miri hide from an older brother in the Vale family's apple shed.
Owen confronts Dr. Vale as Miri, identifies unrelated North Branch photographs as scenes from the invented orchard summer, and is restrained and sedated after screaming that she abandoned him.
The breach establishes that a seven-second fragment can produce a persistent, emotionally coherent alternate childhood and cause unrelated images and people to be incorporated into its narrative.

Incident 97-6 records Owen Bell's fragment exposure, secondary narrative effects in technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth, precautionary observation of contacted pre-cutoff staff, and sealing of the wing.

After Bell's breach, the department destroys the fragment-bearing inspection unit, monitor, cables, hard drive, logs, photographs, and related equipment while leaving the original cassette secured in place.

Technicians Alina Cho and Peter Wirth begin recalling Owen Bell as an impossible schoolmate and generate additional details of the apple-shed childhood; Cho questions why the department is punishing a child for remembering.
Mara warns that the official breach log may itself be an unsafe artifact because its descriptive details could reconstruct the narrative in later readers.

Following Incident 97-6, Vale imposes stricter containment rules prohibiting descriptive discussion of unapproved media, personal names in exposed-subject interviews, and unsupervised handwritten records.

Junior Facilities employee Nia Bellweather, born in 2000 and never directly exposed to the fragment, develops recurring dreams of the constructed hiding-place narrative after hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading part of the breach log.
Daniel states that he wants to remember Lily without being believed, while Mara writes an approved archival sentence asserting that a constructed memory can be false without being meaningless.

Vale formally proposes burying AM-97-441 beneath North Branch in a reinforced ceramic-lined chamber and placing severely affected subjects in indefinite neurological isolation, citing propagation risk and failed ordinary rehabilitation.
Daniel reports that he can identify factual details about his mother Elena but can no longer visualize her face, while Lily's face remains vivid; he begs Mara to help him find Lily.

Mara challenges Vale before the review board, arguing that indefinite isolation turns protective containment into ownership; the board defers the proposal and authorizes ninety-day renewable subject isolation pending further clinical review.

Mara begins an initial reintegration strategy with Daniel by having him recite verified facts and caring behaviors associated with Elena while acknowledging Lily's emotional significance without treating her as real.

Mara discovers that Elias encountered a cassette labeled HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97 while cataloging unprovenanced VHS material for a Pennsylvania historical society in September 2008; the department classified the exposure as probable and later tracked the tape’s circulation.

Department records reveal that after the 2008 exposure Elias repeatedly described a yellow house, an attic, a summer archive, and a daughter named Ruth, while retaining factual orientation but developing severe affective contradiction around his family history.

Mara learns that the Department knew Elias was exposed and knew of Ruth before her own involvement, yet withheld the family-linked records and classified his refusal of correction as uncooperative noncompliance.

Mara reconstructs Elias Venn’s post-exposure decline through receipts, letters, a notebook, and appointment notes, finding a temporal link between the 2008 tape encounter and his search for the yellow house and Ruth.

Elias’s recovered records show he retained factual recognition of Mara while accusing her of helping the wrong family erase Ruth, demonstrating that his anomalous beliefs coexisted with alcohol-related symptoms and probable dementia.

Mara records an approved assessment that Elias was factually unreliable but emotionally consequential and that his decline was temporally linked to probable AM-97-441 exposure, accepting that he was wrong about Ruth without dismissing what happened to him.

Saira tells Mara that Elias searched three possible yellow-house properties but no physical property associated with the tape was confirmed, and that records from his later November evaluation remain unrecovered.

Mara discovers Elias’s concealed final letter, in which he acknowledges Ruth was not real, identifies the tape’s gift as a memory of being the attentive father he wanted to be, apologizes for accusing Mara, and warns that the anomaly lies about what people deserve to have happened rather than simply what happened.

Mara formally records that Elias’s emotional attachment to Ruth and his idealized paternal self remain consequential without establishing Ruth as factual, and she preserves the letter separately under department supervision.

Mara and Saira locate restricted Palinode Institute files identifying AM-97-441 as residual media from a behavioral program intended to manufacture belonging and voluntary political compliance through shared but individualized childhood nostalgia.

Palinode’s final-phase documents establish that researchers used private emotional absence, consumer VHS conventions, and flexible autobiographical prompts rather than identical memories, with a yellow-sided house appearing as a recurring legitimacy symbol.

Saira tells Mara that Palinode’s objective was obedience experienced as kinship, while Mara records that affected people are not the program’s purpose and preserves the statement beside Elias’s letter under separate seal.

Mara studies a controlled Palinode methodology file documenting visual entrainment, VHS defects, guided recollection, memory drugs, social reinforcement, and flexible emotional templates that caused subjects to generate incompatible families and seek to inhabit constructed childhoods.

Mara concludes that AM-97-441 may be a calibration reel designed to make viewers supply their own emotional absences and autobiographical details, rather than a conventional home movie with fixed content.

Palinode case records reveal exposed subjects abandoning legal identities, pursuing constructed homes and families, and treating resistance to reintegration as evidence of successful attachment; one case is linked to the previously reviewed pantry testimony.
Mara begins using a non-descriptive fact-based grounding gesture with Daniel, prompting him to remain oriented to the present without denying Lily’s emotional significance.

Saira gives Mara restricted access to the 1997 anchor-date file, establishing that July 19, 1997 was selected as a functional temporal anchor for consumer VHS distribution rather than as a historically significant date.

The Palinode final phase planned to seed mass-market VHS tapes through thrift shops, estate sales, church rummage events, and liquidation auctions, disguising calibration material as discovered home movies.

During the July 19, 1997 comparison trial, technician R. Bell was exposed and identified laboratory director Adrian Kessler as her deceased son Matthew; the incident escalated into a fire that officially closed the Palinode Institute, with Kessler presumed dead and Bell later dying under prolonged sedation.

After the Palinode fire, attempted destruction of surviving cassettes and equipment produced anomalous persistence, including replay after erasure, self-rewound tape, and a seven-second audio loop from furnace ash, leading the department to suspend ordinary disposal.

The Department of Anomalous Media inherited surviving Palinode consumer cassettes, research notes, and damaged playback equipment, separating the material among secure sites and placing the presumed source in suspension.

Saira shares Daniel’s latest assessments, which recommend controlled symbolic integration: subjects may retain emotionally significant constructed figures while distinguishing literal belief from personal meaning.

During a supervised grounding session, Daniel identifies verified facts about his Newark upbringing and mother Elena, acknowledges Lily did not exist as his sister, and identifies Lily’s hand on his shoulder during an unverified thunderstorm memory as representing someone who knew he was afraid.

Dr. Irena Vale reveals that an earlier anomalous-media exposure in her family home in 1981 fractured her parents’ and brother Paul’s autobiographical identities, destroyed the family’s relationships, and left Paul unable to recognize her for decades.

Vale identifies the earlier household tape as a pre-VHS calibration medium with behavior matching AM-97-441; her father’s destruction attempt produced radio playback from the ash, linking her personal history to Palinode-type persistence.

Owen Bell accurately reproduces private details of Vale’s real apple shed and family repairs, including the swollen west door, copper-wire hinge, green blanket, late-blooming tree, and red ribbon, despite not having access to her records.

Mara argues that AM-97-441 may assemble narrative fragments from nearby people rather than merely parasitize an individual host, and Vale orders her family details source-isolated and removes the phrase apple shed from the active incident summary.

Mara and Saira secretly establish an unauthorized plan to use the tape transfer as a controlled confrontation, with informed consent, pre-cutoff interviewers, signal severance, and separate post-contact grounding rooms.
Daniel explicitly consents to confront the constructed material after being told it is unsafe and stoppable, while retaining factual anchors and requesting one fact-based interview afterward.

Owen Bell gives qualified spoken consent to confront his constructed childhood after being informed that Miri may not be real and that the signal can be stopped, though his understanding remains unstable.
Saira prepares and memorizes a transfer route from the medical wing through the vault to the burial elevator, including separate interview and emergency sedation rooms, then destroys the route map.

Vale discovers a faint unauthorized vault-access impression bearing Saira Okafor’s initials, treats it as evidence of procedural compromise, and accelerates the source transfer and burial to 14:00 the same day.
Vale removes Saira from medical-wing and vault duties, suspends her clearance, and assigns her to source-isolated administrative work pending review.
Vale orders Daniel transferred from Room Four to a more isolated neurological unit with no shared ventilation, plumbing, or staff rotation, despite acknowledging that he has committed no infraction.

Mara establishes that the Department has no discharge criteria, reintegration schedule, family counseling, legal advocacy, or long-term care plan for subjects whose factual memories remain accessible while emotional attachments have been displaced.

Vale’s burial memorandum states that once AM-97-441 is buried, active studies of symbolic integration, emotional retention, and post-exposure reintegration will be suspended, revealing burial as both containment and institutional closure of the ethical debate.

During the accelerated burial, the elevator stops between floors and the mechanical playback deck activates without authorization even after the output relay and building intercom breakers are disconnected.
AM-97-441 audio propagates through the North Branch intercom and emergency devices as static, children’s laughter, pool water, and distant voices despite the facility’s severance attempts.

Personnel born after the vulnerability cutoff begin perceiving personalized childhood locations and recasting coworkers as relatives, teachers, enemies, and lost friends, causing the lockdown and identity checks to fail across the mill.
Mara and Saira reestablish contact through their prearranged three-two-three knocking pattern, confirming that the burial order remains incomplete while the source continues activating the facility.

During the active transfer breach, vulnerable personnel perceive North Branch as individualized summer camps, homes, churches, hospitals, and other childhood settings; facility maps, doors, uniforms, and identities cease to agree across observers, disrupting coordinated security response.

Saira reaches exposed personnel in the emergency corridors and grounds them by repeating their names, birth dates, location, bodily sensations, and other verifiable present facts without arguing with their personalized perceptions.

Mara and Saira, with Vale’s factual confirmation, descend toward the neurological unit and locate Daniel inside a composite yellow-room setting where the anomaly presents a false family and Lily’s voice urges Mara that she has arrived too late.

Inside the composite yellow room, Daniel encounters Lily as an older girl who identifies herself as the part of him that has waited for someone to admit his loneliness, rather than as a literal sister trapped in the tape.

Mara and Saira ground Daniel with verifiable facts about his Newark upbringing, Elena, Rutgers, and North Branch; Daniel acknowledges his loneliness, consents to remain in the present, and refuses to follow Lily into the constructed yellow house while retaining love for what she represents.

During the active breach, Mara experiences Ruth as a lost sister beside Elias, then recognizes the figure’s face and details as an assembled construction using her childhood photographs, Daniel’s Lily descriptions, and Palinode’s yellow-house conventions; she rejects calling Ruth factual while preserving the grief as emotionally real.

Through the unstable relay, Mara, Saira, and Daniel view Palinode’s final research recording, which identifies the program’s goal as using nostalgia to make subjects surrender the present to whoever defines the past and confirms that adaptive longing produced individualized counterfeit childhoods instead of ideological consensus.

The Palinode recording warns that conventional destruction and burial may not be neutral, distinguishes emotional persistence from factual validity, and instructs future handlers to record the subject’s want while rejecting the authority attached to it.

The unstable relay reaches the end of the recording and immediately begins again, while the disconnected vault reel continues turning and the yellow-house image remains active, confirming that the source can cycle its final sequence without a functioning conventional motor.

Mara, Saira, and Daniel prevent Vale’s blind incineration order, interrupt the suspension-locker transfer, and route AM-97-441’s active output into a localized inspection channel instead of the facility intercom.
Vale authorizes the controlled channel while retaining destruction as a witnessed contingency; pre-cutoff personnel move exposed staff away from the relay and begin grounding and subject checks.

The first controlled inspection-channel interviews are conducted under informed consent, with each subject stating present verifiable facts before being invited to distinguish an emotional truth from the constructed childhood narrative.

Daniel identifies Lily as a constructed figure and says she represents the person he invented so he would not be the only one who knew he was lonely; he stops after eleven minutes and requests that the record note he stopped rather than failed.

Alina Cho identifies the constructed school narrative as representing the wish that someone could disappear while people still remembered him, and asks that her memory of being treated kindly be preserved without asserting Owen Bell was factually her classmate.

Peter Wirth identifies the constructed hiding place as representing a place where fear meant someone would come, but rejects the interview framework and accuses the department of stealing his proof that anyone would come.

Mara's handwritten source-isolated notes establish that factual correction does not dissolve attachment, grief survives recognition, and testimony can remain precise without granting a constructed narrative authority.

In the controlled inspection interviews, the lakeside-camp subject acknowledges that her grandmother associated with Camp Halcyon never lived, while choosing to retain her as a named internal story without making a factual claim.

The former foster-care subject rejects the belief that Helen Kessler stole him, but retains the constructed pantry memory as part of his identity and as a representation of wanting protection; he asks the record to distinguish his own change from departmental correction.
Alina Cho accepts that Owen Bell was not factually her schoolmate while insisting that the kindness she remembers remains an event in her own emotional life.

Peter Wirth refuses symbolic-integration language, demands that the department acknowledge the concrete-room memory as part of his identity without calling it factual, and declines consent for another interview.
Mara and Saira amend the rights ledger to distinguish factual status from subject meaning and to preserve subjects' own language about retained constructed memories.

During a supervised interview, Owen Bell distinguishes Dr. Irena Vale from Miri, identifying Miri as the protective part of himself formed by the constructed childhood; he accepts continued supervision without forced erasure while retaining the apple-shed memory as nonliteral and emotionally meaningful.

Dr. Vale revises Bell’s clinical classification from noncompliant to subject under supervision, documenting emerging factual distinction, retained emotional attachment, and neither cure nor total loss.

During a supervised session, Daniel recounts verifiable details of his Newark apartment and Elena’s practical care, recognizes that his adolescent loneliness was real without making Lily factual, and distinguishes Elena’s imperfect efforts from the constructed family narrative.

Daniel writes on a paper cup, “Lily is not real,” followed by “I do not have to stop loving her,” and consents in principle to a future call with Elena while postponing it after staff observe excessive emotional and physical strain.

An emergency review suspends Vale’s burial order and replaces indefinite renewable isolation with source-separated supervised care, thirty-day clinical reviews, informed consent, independent oversight, and individual long-term care plans.

AM-97-441 is resealed without playback in a secondary ceramic housing with independent grounding, mechanical status indication, and physically separated service systems; the playback deck is removed for witnessed disposition and no copies are made.

Mara and Saira create a paper rights ledger separating independently verifiable facts from subject-owned emotional meaning, preserving affected subjects’ statements and refusals without descriptive reproduction.

future_requirements.description: Daniel and Elena must complete a medically supervised call in which Daniel explains Lily’s nonliteral emotional significance and preserves contact with his mother.
Vale must resign after refusing to recognize Daniel’s retained memories as anything beyond contamination, and Saira must assume leadership of the revised care-and-containment program.

character_states.name: Mara Venn
character_states.description: At the close of the chapter, Mara has returned from Elias Venn’s grave to the North Branch paper mill under her monitored consultant status. She remains physically tired but factually oriented as a pre-cutoff consultant born March 4, 1985, with supervised paper, pencil, gloves, and department clothing but no personal possessions. She knows AM-97-441 remains resealed without playback in the source-isolated vault and continues supporting humane containment, separate factual status from subject-owned emotional meaning, and advocate for affected subjects’ autonomy. She has completed the supervised call between Daniel and Elena and left Elias a note affirming his grief and the father he wanted to be while refusing to make Ruth factual. She remains emotionally burdened but more reconciled to Elias’s suffering.

character_states.name: Daniel Reyes
character_states.description: In Room Four-B of the North Branch supervised medical wing after a medically supervised eleven-minute call, Daniel remains exhausted but oriented, born June 17, 1993. He has no personal possessions except the paper cup bearing his statement that Lily is not real and that he does not have to stop loving her. He can state his Newark upbringing, living mother Elena, Rutgers education, current location, and the concrete childhood memories Elena shared. He understands Lily as a symbolic companion representing the family and witness he needed rather than a factual sister, and has told Elena this distinction without accusing her. He voluntarily ended the call, wants future contact and a possible visit under renewed consent, and requires compassionate grounding without forced erasure.

character_states.name: Len
character_states.description: At Sal’s Second Chance thrift shop on Route 219 in rural Pennsylvania, Len remains the dismissive seller of HOME MOVIE—SUMMER ’97. He has no known provenance records for the cassette and remains unaware that its playback caused Daniel’s implanted memories, Mara’s exposure, and Department intervention. He is physically well and mildly irritated by Mara’s earlier questions.

character_states.name: Elias Venn
character_states.description: Deceased father of Mara Venn, buried in a Lutheran cemetery in a Pennsylvania town. His final letter and Mara’s grave note now preserve a distinction between factual error and emotional consequence: Ruth was not real, but Elias genuinely grieved and remembered the father he could have been. His exposure, decline, alcoholism, probable dementia, accusations, and concealed apology remain part of Mara’s understanding of AM-97-441’s harm. No new possessions or living location apply; the grave and separately preserved letter are his remaining material traces.

character_states.name: Elena Reyes
character_states.description: At her New Jersey home, Elena remains Daniel’s living mother and emergency contact, frightened but protective. During the medically supervised call she listened as Daniel explained that Lily never existed as a sister but remains emotionally meaningful, and she responded by sharing concrete memories of his childhood and acknowledging both his effort and the reality of his loneliness without validating Lily as factual. She agreed to wait for a medically cleared, consent-based future visit or call. She remains unaware of the Department’s full containment history and has not possessed the tape or altered artifacts.

character_states.name: Saira Okafor
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, source-isolated records area, vault control station, and director’s office, Saira is fatigued but physically capable, born October 12, 1978. She has assumed the director role of the revised Anomalous Media Care and Containment Program after Vale’s resignation. She possesses supervised paper, pencil, gloves, authorized control materials, the revised clinical standard, and the rights ledger. She is responsible for source separation, informed consent, thirty-day clinical reviews, independent oversight, long-term care plans, and preserving subject-owned meaning without factual certification. She continues monitoring Daniel, Owen, Alina, Peter, Nia, and other affected personnel and intends to maintain containment as care rather than punishment.

character_states.name: Dr. Irena Vale
character_states.description: After refusing to sign the revised clinical standard, Vale has resigned from the North Branch directorate and surrendered her director’s badge and vault-access authority. She remains factually oriented as a pre-cutoff specialist born in 1969, emotionally exhausted and defensive, and may remain available to the department for source-security or historical review without directing the revised care program. She still believes retained constructed memories are contamination and considers the new framework dangerously permissive, though she has witnessed Saira assume public responsibility. She has no authority over Daniel’s care or the resealed source and is preparing to leave her former office.

character_states.name: Owen Bell
character_states.description: In Room Seven of the North Branch supervised medical wing, Owen remains intermittently sedated but awake and medically monitored, born in 1993, with no personal possessions except the paper cup on which he wrote Miri. He can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, and distinguishes Dr. Irena Vale from Miri, the protective identity formed within the constructed childhood. His apple-shed memories remain nonliteral but emotionally meaningful. He remains a supervised-care subject under Saira’s revised program, source-separated, and protected from forced erasure.

character_states.name: Thomas Keene
character_states.description: At the North Branch paper mill, pre-cutoff orderly Thomas Keene remains unsteady but conscious after helping restrain Owen Bell. He can state his verified identity, birth date, and location, though he experienced a transient sensation of having forgotten a summer. During the emergency he repeated his identity anchors and helped move exposed staff away from the relay under Saira’s direction. He has no confirmed lasting memory alteration, no possessions, and remains under medical observation and grounding protocols.

character_states.name: Alina Cho
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room supervised medical area, Alina remains frightened but verbally settled and source-separated, born February 3, 1994, with no personal possessions. She can state her identity, work in facilities, scar on her left thumb, and location. She accepts that Owen Bell was not factually her schoolmate while insisting that the kindness she remembers remains an event in her own emotional life. She has dictated that distinction into the new rights ledger, remains under psychological and medical observation, and may refuse further interviews.

character_states.name: Peter Wirth
character_states.description: In the North Branch west-room supervised medical area, Peter remains agitated and emotionally defensive, born November 9, 1994, with a bandaged hand and no personal possessions. He can state that his sister Rebecca lives in Ohio and that the concrete-room childhood is not factually verifiable, though he still cannot reliably picture Rebecca’s face. He rejects symbolic-integration language, demands acknowledgment that the constructed memory is part of his identity without calling it factual, and has refused to dictate a meaning statement beyond recording his refusal. He remains source-separated and entitled to clinical care, review, and independent advocacy.

character_states.name: Nia Bellweather
character_states.description: Nia remains isolated for seventy-two hours in a medical room at North Branch under nighttime sedation and pre-cutoff clinical supervision. Born in 2000, she never directly viewed AM-97-441 or the unauthorized fragment and has not viewed the Palinode final recording. After hearing an emotionally detailed account and reading two lines of the breach log, she continues recurring dreams of an unnamed outbuilding, wet wood, breathing beneath a floor, and a waiting child. She believes the dream belongs to her but has not established it as factual; her account remains potentially unsafe and she possesses no personal materials.
