character_states.name: Irena
character_states.description: Irena is behind the collapsing iron gate at the submerged crypt, bracing it while protecting Tomas and the surviving patients. Her altered seam reaches nearly to her elbow and she carries her rusted blade; she ignited Elias's blood-and-oil rite with the lantern flame and is now determined to get the survivors out as the foundations fail. She knows Elias's fate is uncertain and has not abandoned him emotionally, but must prioritize the living.

past_events.description: Elias accepted Governor Rook's commission and departed for Saint Orison's aboard the launch Mercy during the storm.
Elias retained his old damp prayer book and a tarnished silver crucifix when leaving the parish house.
Elias arrived at Saint Orison's during the storm and confirmed that the island was cut off after the radio mast was destroyed.
Elias inspected three bodies: Warden Pell folded into a kneeling shape, patient Dorr altered with sewn skin, and Nurse Elsie Marr drowned with seawater despite being found in Ward C.
Governor Rook privately admitted that Saint Orison's records had been altered and that staff members were missing without being listed as dead.
Patients at Saint Orison's called Elias 'Father of the Door' and claimed that his little girl was waiting, linking the asylum's terror to Mara.
In the oldest ward, mute patient Tomas Bell spoke in Matron Vey’s voice and accused the asylum of drugging, bleeding, and burying patients beneath the chapel.
Irena showed Elias teeth hidden in her mattress and claimed they belonged to living people whose faces or bodies had changed.
Restrained patient Hobb briefly grew the hands of dead Warden Pell and strangled himself; Elias disrupted the transformation with his silver crucifix.
Elias found punishment schedules documenting Father Orison’s fasting, bloodletting, salt-kneeling, and shackled devotional treatments.

Elias found a damaged founder’s ledger describing a black bone called the Adversary’s relic, recovered from the wreck of the Mercy Bell and sealed beneath the chapel after changing worshippers’ flesh.
Elias heard Mara’s childhood hymn in an empty corridor and followed wet child-sized footprints toward the chapel stair, where the hymn continued beneath the floor.
Elias and Irena entered the hidden archive through a passage behind the laundry cistern and found preserved organs labeled with the names of recent victims.
The founder's ledger revealed that Orison's apparent miracles involved flesh-changing bargains and that the recent victims were marked for their roles in concealing or enabling the asylum's abuses.
Rook admitted he was commissioned to destroy evidence before a mainland inspection and confirmed that the relic remained beneath the chapel after someone recently opened its crypt.
A false figure wearing Saye's face attacked Elias in the chapel, collapsed into hair, teeth, and drowned clothing, and triggered a clapperless bell beneath the floor.
The chapel floor collapsed, revealing stairs into the monastery foundations; Elias, Irena, and Saye descended while the asylum shook above them.
In underground chambers, Elias and his companions found preserved organs labeled with patients' names, including a fresh heart labeled Agnes Vey.
Elias confessed that Mara had asked him to stop during her exorcism, that he recognized her voice, and that he continued because he feared disobeying Bishop Haldane more than losing her.
The black-white bone relic awakened and released the Mercy Below, which identified itself as invited by human cruelty and moved through Saye, Irena, and an imitation of Mara.
The awakened presence animated the dead into a crawling congregation and sealed the crypt, forcing Elias and Irena to flee as Saint Orison's foundations began shifting.
The Mercy Below spread through the wards, reshaping patients, corpses, and staff and causing the asylum's corridors to rearrange according to fear.
Dr. Saye's overtaken body offered Elias limitless scientific knowledge while displaying multiple unstable faces and organs.
Elias and Irena found surviving patients hiding in the laundry tunnels, where Matron Vey admitted she had offered people to the Mercy Below as salvation.
Matron Vey's body divided into six saintlike forms speaking contradictory prayers, and she revealed that the Mercy Below requires a willing flesh vessel to cross the sea.
The Mercy Below confronted Elias through multiple manifestations of Mara and blamed his obedience for opening the door to her death.

The Mercy Below separated Elias from the patients and forced him through visions of the tribunal, Mara's death, and his younger self's cowardice; Elias rejected the interpretations that made him a martyr or absolved him through obedience.
Rook attempted to deliver Elias to the Mercy Below after accepting its promise to erase his political crimes, but the entity transformed him into a mass of official seals, teeth, and grasping hands.
The transformed Rook shot Elias in the shoulder before being overcome, leaving Elias wounded but able to continue.
Dr. Saye recovered Father Orison's notes stating that the relic can be destroyed by fire made from consecrated oil mixed with the blood of a person who confesses without asking forgiveness.
Elias accepted that he must serve as the willing vessel and enter the fire without treating sacrifice as a purchase of forgiveness.
Elias publicly confessed before the surviving patients that he heard Mara ask him to stop, abandoned her, lied about it, and pursued punishment instead of repentance.
Irena cut her altered hand to demonstrate that the Mercy Below can imitate pain but cannot understand freely chosen sacrifice, disrupting its imitation of Mara.
Dr. Saye obtained the consecrated oil, then held back the transformed staff in the chapel treasury so Elias and Irena could descend with it toward the relic.
In the submerged crypt, Elias rejected the Mercy Below's nihilism and the Church's certainty, choosing the rite without claiming that it would earn forgiveness or save anyone.
Elias mixed his blood with consecrated oil, confessed without asking forgiveness, and drove the black bone relic into his chest as the willing vessel.
Irena ignited the blood-and-oil fire through the gate, and the Mercy Below began tearing through Elias toward the storm drain as the crypt collapsed.

future_requirements.description: Elias must confront manifestations of Mara and recognize that his guilt, rather than supernatural mystery alone, is the wound the Mercy exploits.
Elias and the surviving patients must reach the old sea gate while the Mercy Below continues reshaping the asylum.
Irena must lead the surviving patients through the collapsing asylum to the old sea gate and toward a mainland rescue vessel after the storm weakens.
The aftermath must leave Elias's fate uncertain while preserving his confession as the surviving moral evidence of Saint Orison's crimes.

character_states.name: Elias Vale
character_states.description: Elias is presumed dead or transformed beneath the collapsed, submerged chapel crypt. He forced the Mercy Below and the burning relic into the reliquary and sealed it with his own hands, but no body was recovered. His confession survives in his damaged prayer book; his tarnished crucifix and final physical fate are unknown. His last known goal was to prevent the entity from escaping through the storm drains without using sacrifice to purchase forgiveness.

character_states.name: Silas Rook
character_states.description: Rook is missing and presumed destroyed or buried in the collapsing asylum after transforming into official seals, teeth, and grasping hands. His pistol, commission, and bureaucratic flesh were left somewhere in Saint Orison's ruins. He remains an unresolved symbol of the institutional cover-up, with no confirmed surviving identity.

character_states.name: Mara Venn
character_states.description: Mara remains dead. The Mercy Below used her face and voice during Elias's final confrontation, but Elias refused to use the imitation again and no genuine fragment or resurrection was established. Her memory survives in Elias's confession and in the childhood hymn associated with her.

character_states.name: Dr. Lucien Saye
character_states.description: Saye is presumed dead or lost beneath the collapsing chapel treasury after holding back the transformed staff so Elias and Irena could obtain the consecrated oil. His notes enabled the destruction rite, but his body and survival remain unconfirmed.

character_states.name: Agnes Vey
character_states.description: Vey is missing and presumed drowned, buried, or still fused with the transformed staff after the asylum collapsed. Her six saintlike forms had served the Mercy Below and sought to deliver survivors to its promised salvation. No confirmed trace of her remains outside the sea-washed ruins.

character_states.name: Irena
character_states.description: Irena escaped Saint Orison's through the old sea gate with Tomas and the surviving patients, reaching the breakwater before a mainland rescue vessel arrived. She carries Elias's damaged prayer book and rusted blade, retains the altered seam on her arm, and knows his fate is uncertain. She remains emotionally burdened by his disappearance while guarding the truth preserved in his confession.
